writing.title: Four-day working week
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Some people believe that a four-day working week would benefit both employees and employers.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: nêu xu hướng thử nghiệm tuần làm 4 ngày + quan điểm: phần lớn đồng ý, nhưng tuỳ ngành
Thân 1: lợi ích cho nhân viên – nghỉ ngơi, giảm stress/burnout, ít nghỉ ốm
Thân 2: lợi ích cho công ty – năng suất giữ nguyên, thu hút và giữ chân người giỏi
Thân 3 (giới hạn): ngành phải hoạt động cả tuần (bệnh viện, cửa hàng) → lịch linh hoạt
Kết bài: 'win-win' nếu được điều chỉnh theo từng ngành
vocab: tình trạng kiệt sức vì công việc
An extra day off can significantly reduce stress and burnout.
Staff tend to cut down on unproductive meetings.
It helps companies recruit and retain talented staff.
A shorter week is an attractive perk.
giải pháp dung hoà thực tế
A flexible schedule may be a more realistic compromise.
cách sắp xếp đôi bên cùng có lợi
It is generally a win-win arrangement.
writing.sample:
In recent years, several companies have experimented with reducing the working week to four days without cutting salaries. Some argue that this arrangement serves the interests of both workers and businesses. I largely agree with this view, although its success depends on the type of work involved.

For employees, the advantages are fairly obvious. An extra day off gives people more time to rest, look after their families and pursue interests outside work, which can significantly reduce stress and burnout. In countries where trials have taken place, many participants reported sleeping better and feeling more motivated when they returned to work. A healthier, happier workforce is also likely to take fewer sick days.

Employers can benefit as well. When staff know they have only four days to complete their tasks, they tend to cut down on unproductive meetings and distractions, so overall output often remains stable. Moreover, a shorter week is an attractive perk that helps companies recruit and retain talented staff without raising wages, which can save considerable recruitment and training costs.

That said, the model is not suitable for every sector. Hospitals, shops and public transport must operate every day, so a four-day week for individual workers would require hiring additional staff or reorganising shifts, which could raise costs. In such cases, a flexible schedule may be a more realistic compromise.

In conclusion, I believe a four-day working week is generally a win-win arrangement, improving employees' well-being while maintaining or even boosting productivity, provided that it is adapted to the needs of each industry.

writing.title: Can AI replace teachers?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Artificial intelligence will soon be able to replace teachers in the classroom.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: AI phát triển nhanh + quan điểm: hoàn toàn không đồng ý
Thân 1 (nhượng bộ): AI làm tốt vài việc – cá nhân hoá bài tập, phản hồi tức thì, chấm bài
Thân 2: dạy học cần đồng cảm, động viên, quản lý lớp, dạy kỹ năng xã hội
Thân 3: nguy cơ học sinh thụ động, phụ thuộc vào AI vốn có thể sai
Kết bài: AI là trợ lý của giáo viên chứ không thay thế
vocab: học tập thích ứng (tự điều chỉnh theo người học)
Adaptive learning programs can identify a student's weaknesses.
sự đồng cảm và khả năng phán đoán
These tasks depend on empathy and judgement.
sự phụ thuộc quá mức vào
There is a risk of over-reliance on technology.
writing.sample:
Rapid advances in artificial intelligence have led some people to predict that machines will soon take over the role of classroom teachers. While AI is certain to change education, I strongly disagree that it can replace human teachers.

Admittedly, AI tools already perform some teaching tasks remarkably well. Adaptive learning programs can identify a student's weaknesses, provide instant feedback and adjust the difficulty of exercises, something a single teacher with forty pupils cannot always do. AI can also mark multiple-choice tests and answer routine questions at any hour, freeing teachers from repetitive work.

However, teaching involves far more than delivering information. Teachers motivate reluctant learners, notice when a child is anxious or unhappy, and manage the complex social dynamics of a classroom. These tasks depend on empathy and judgement, qualities that machines do not possess. Furthermore, schools play a key role in teaching young people how to cooperate, resolve conflicts and behave responsibly, and such skills are best learned through relationships with real adults.

There is also the risk of over-reliance on technology. If students learn mainly from screens, they may become passive and less able to think critically about the answers an AI system gives them, especially since these systems can make mistakes. Children from poorer families, who may lack reliable devices or internet access at home, could also fall further behind.

In conclusion, although artificial intelligence will become a valuable assistant in the classroom, it cannot replace the human qualities that make teachers effective. The most likely future is one in which teachers use AI to support, rather than replace, their work.

writing.title: Banning private cars from city centres
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Private cars should be banned from city centres.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: kẹt xe, ô nhiễm ở trung tâm + quan điểm: đồng ý một phần (hạn chế thay vì cấm hẳn)
Thân 1: lợi ích – không khí sạch, phố đi bộ, công viên, cửa hàng địa phương hưởng lợi
Thân 2: bất cập của lệnh cấm hoàn toàn – người già, người khuyết tật, thợ cần xe; giao thông công cộng kém
Thân 3: giải pháp từng bước – phí ùn tắc, hạn chế bãi đỗ, miễn trừ, đầu tư xe buýt và làn xe đạp
Kết bài: nên giảm xe cá nhân; chỉ cấm hẳn khi có phương án thay thế tốt
vocab: Roads could be turned into pedestrian zones.
An outright ban is only justified when good public transport exists.
They could allow exemptions for essential users.
It would damage the city centre rather than revitalise it.
writing.sample:
Many city centres suffer from heavy traffic, noise and air pollution, and some people believe the solution is to ban private cars from these areas entirely. I partly agree: restricting cars in central districts is sensible, but a complete ban would be unfair to certain groups unless strong alternatives are in place.

There are clear benefits to keeping cars out of city centres. Fewer vehicles mean cleaner air and quieter streets, which improves public health and makes walking and cycling more pleasant. Space currently used for roads and parking could be turned into pedestrian zones, parks and outdoor cafés, as several European cities have done. Local businesses often benefit too, because people on foot tend to stop and shop more than those driving through.

However, a total ban could cause hardship. Elderly and disabled residents may depend on cars to reach hospitals or shops, and tradespeople need vehicles to carry tools and materials. In cities with poor public transport, banning cars would simply make it harder for people to get to work, damaging the economy of the centre rather than revitalising it.

Therefore, a gradual and flexible approach seems wiser. Authorities could introduce congestion charges, limit parking and create car-free streets, while allowing exemptions for essential users. At the same time, they should invest in frequent, affordable buses and safe cycle lanes.

In conclusion, reducing private car use in city centres is desirable, but an outright ban is only justified when good public transport exists and the needs of vulnerable groups are protected.

writing.title: A tax on sugary food and drinks
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Governments should put a tax on sugary food and drinks in order to reduce obesity.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: béo phì tăng, gánh nặng y tế + quan điểm: đồng ý, nếu là một phần chiến lược rộng hơn
Thân 1: giá ảnh hưởng hành vi; nhà sản xuất giảm đường trong sản phẩm
Thân 2: tiền thuế dùng cho y tế cộng đồng – thể thao, bữa ăn học đường, giáo dục dinh dưỡng
Thân 3 (phản biện): thuế 'đánh' vào người nghèo, hạn chế tự do → miễn thuế thực phẩm cơ bản, trợ giá rau quả
Kết bài: biện pháp hợp lý và hiệu quả
vocab: Obesity places great pressure on healthcare systems.
Manufacturers reformulate their drinks to contain less sugar.
The revenue can be reinvested in public health.
bệnh liên quan đến chế độ ăn
Poorer communities suffer most from diet-related diseases.
giải quyết vấn đề béo phì
It tackles obesity from several directions at once.
writing.sample:
Obesity rates have risen sharply in many countries, placing great pressure on healthcare systems. One proposed response is to tax products that are high in sugar. I agree that such a tax is a sensible measure, provided it forms part of a wider strategy.

The main argument for a sugar tax is that price influences behaviour. When sugary drinks become more expensive, consumers tend to buy fewer of them or switch to healthier alternatives such as water. In addition, the tax encourages manufacturers to reformulate their products with less sugar to avoid paying more, which benefits everyone, including people who never read nutrition labels. Several countries that introduced such taxes have seen popular soft drinks become noticeably less sweet.

Another advantage is that the money raised can be reinvested in public health. Governments could use it to fund sports facilities, healthier school meals or campaigns about diet, tackling obesity from several directions at once.

Critics argue that the tax punishes poorer families, who spend a larger share of their income on food, and that it limits personal freedom. These concerns are understandable, but they can be addressed by keeping basic foods tax-free and using the revenue to make fresh fruit and vegetables cheaper. Moreover, poorer communities often suffer most from diet-related diseases, so they also stand to gain the most.

In conclusion, I believe taxing sugary products is a justified and effective way to reduce obesity, especially if the revenue is spent on making healthy choices easier and more affordable.

writing.title: Free entry to museums and galleries
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Museums and art galleries should be free for everyone to visit.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: tranh luận về vé vào cửa + quan điểm: bảo tàng công nên miễn phí, triển lãm đặc biệt có thể thu phí
Thân 1: văn hoá là của chung; phí làm người thu nhập thấp, học sinh ngại đến; ví dụ Anh bỏ vé → khách tăng mạnh
Thân 2: miễn phí khuyến khích ghé thăm nhiều lần, gắn bó lâu dài với văn hoá
Thân 3 (nhượng bộ): cần tiền vận hành → ngân sách, tài trợ, quán cà phê, cửa hàng, phí triển lãm tạm thời
Kết bài: lợi ích xã hội và giáo dục lớn hơn khoản thu từ vé
vocab: Museums hold a nation's shared heritage.
National museums in the UK abolished admission charges.
People may drop in for half an hour during a lunch break.
Culture should not be an expensive one-off outing.
Alternative sources of funding must be secured.
writing.sample:
Whether museums and galleries should charge entrance fees is a long-running debate. In my view, public museums should be free to enter, although charging for special exhibitions is a reasonable way to support their finances.

The strongest argument for free entry is that culture belongs to everyone. Museums hold a nation's shared heritage, and entrance fees, even modest ones, discourage low-income families, students and young people from visiting. When national museums in the UK abolished admission charges, visitor numbers rose dramatically, showing how strongly price affects access. Free museums can also become valuable educational spaces where children develop curiosity about history, science and art outside the classroom.

In addition, free entry encourages repeat and casual visits. People who do not have to pay are more likely to drop in for half an hour during a lunch break or return several times to see different galleries, building a long-term relationship with culture rather than treating it as an expensive one-off outing. Tourists who enter for free are also likely to spend money in museum shops and cafés, which benefits the wider local economy.

Admittedly, museums need money to maintain buildings, protect collections and stage exhibitions, and taxpayers who never visit may object to funding them. However, this can be managed through government grants, donations, cafés, gift shops and charges for temporary exhibitions, while the permanent collections remain open to all.

In conclusion, I largely agree that museums and galleries should be free, because the social and educational benefits of wider access outweigh the lost ticket revenue, provided alternative sources of funding are secured.

writing.title: Social media and false information
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Social media companies should be held responsible for the false information that is shared on their platforms.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: tin giả gây hại + quan điểm: đồng ý phần lớn, trách nhiệm chia sẻ với người dùng và chính phủ
Thân 1: nền tảng không trung lập – thuật toán đẩy nội dung giật gân để kiếm tiền → phải gắn nhãn, gỡ tài khoản giả
Thân 2: chỉ công ty có năng lực kỹ thuật xử lý nhanh, quy mô lớn; trách nhiệm pháp lý tạo động lực kiểm duyệt
Thân 3 (giới hạn): phạt quá nặng → gỡ cả ý kiến hợp pháp, đe doạ tự do ngôn luận; người dùng cần hiểu biết truyền thông
Kết bài: chịu trách nhiệm phần lớn nhưng cân bằng với tự do ngôn luận và giáo dục
vocab: nội dung giật gân và gây hiểu lầm
Algorithms often promote sensational and misleading content.
người/tổ chức kiểm chứng thông tin
Fact-checkers have shown the content to be false.
Companies should be made legally accountable.
They would invest in better content moderation.
năng lực hiểu biết truyền thông
writing.sample:
The spread of false information online has become a serious problem, influencing elections and public health decisions and even provoking violence. Some believe that social media companies should be held responsible for this content. I agree to a large extent, although responsibility should be shared with users and governments.

Social media companies are not neutral channels. Their algorithms decide which posts millions of people see, and these systems often promote sensational and misleading content because it attracts more clicks and advertising revenue. Since the companies profit from this attention, it is reasonable to expect them to take action, for example by labelling doubtful posts, removing fake accounts and reducing the reach of content that fact-checkers have shown to be false.

Furthermore, only these firms have the technical ability to act quickly and on a large scale. Individual users cannot check every post they see, and governments are often too slow to keep up with fast-moving online trends. Making companies legally accountable would give them a strong incentive to invest in better content moderation.

However, this responsibility has limits. If platforms are punished too harshly, they may remove legitimate opinions simply to avoid risk, which would threaten freedom of expression. Users also have a duty to think before sharing, and schools should teach media literacy so that people can recognise unreliable sources.

In conclusion, social media companies should be held largely responsible for false information because they design and profit from the systems that spread it, but this must be balanced with protecting free speech and educating the public.

writing.title: Community work instead of prison
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

People who commit minor crimes should do unpaid community work instead of going to prison.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: nhà tù quá tải, tốn kém + quan điểm: hoàn toàn đồng ý với tội nhẹ, không bạo lực
Thân 1: lao động công ích giúp cải tạo – tránh tiếp xúc tội phạm chuyên nghiệp, giữ việc làm và gia đình
Thân 2: lợi ích trực tiếp cho xã hội – tiết kiệm tiền thuế, người phạm tội 'trả lại' cho cộng đồng
Thân 3 (phản biện): 'quá nhẹ' → giám sát chặt, tăng giờ với tái phạm; tội bạo lực vẫn phải ngồi tù
Kết bài: công bằng hơn, rẻ hơn, hiệu quả hơn
vocab: Prisons in many countries are overcrowded.
Community service is more likely to reform offenders.
A criminal record makes it hard to find work.
Offenders give something back to the community.
Some argue community service will not deter crime.
writing.sample:
Prisons in many countries are overcrowded and expensive to run, which has led some people to suggest that minor offenders should perform unpaid community work rather than be locked up. I strongly agree with this approach for non-violent crimes.

Firstly, community service is more likely to reform offenders. Short prison sentences often expose people who have committed small offences, such as shoplifting or vandalism, to more experienced criminals, and they may leave prison with new criminal contacts and a criminal record that makes it hard to find work. By contrast, cleaning parks, repairing public buildings or helping in charity shops allows offenders to keep their jobs and family ties while learning discipline and responsibility.

Secondly, community work benefits society directly. Instead of taxpayers spending large sums to keep someone in prison, offenders give something back to the community they have harmed. This visible form of punishment can also help victims and local residents feel that justice has been done.

Some people argue that community service is too soft and will not deter crime. However, these punishments can be made demanding, with strict supervision and longer hours for repeat offenders, and those who fail to complete their work could still be sent to prison. Of course, this option is only appropriate for minor crimes; violent offenders who threaten public safety must be kept apart from society.

In conclusion, I believe unpaid community work is a fairer, cheaper and more effective punishment than prison for minor, non-violent crimes, as it both reforms offenders and benefits the public.

writing.title: Compulsory internships for university students
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

All university students should be required to complete a work placement before they graduate.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: sinh viên thiếu kinh nghiệm thực tế + quan điểm: phần lớn đồng ý, nhưng phải công bằng
Thân 1: kinh nghiệm thực tế – áp dụng lý thuyết, làm nhóm, deadline; định hướng nghề
Thân 2: tăng khả năng có việc – nhà tuyển dụng ưa kinh nghiệm, mạng lưới quan hệ; trường gắn với doanh nghiệp
Thân 3 (vấn đề): ngành hiếm chỗ thực tập, thực tập không lương bất lợi cho SV nghèo → thực tập có lương, phương án thay thế
Kết bài: nên là chuẩn chung nhưng linh hoạt và có kinh phí
vocab: Every student should complete a work placement.
Students learn how to apply theory to real problems.
xây dựng mạng lưới quan hệ
A placement allows students to build a network of contacts.
bị loại ra, bị bỏ rơi
writing.sample:
Many graduates complain that their degrees have not prepared them for the realities of the workplace. As a result, some people argue that every university student should complete a work placement before graduating. I mostly agree with this idea, although universities must ensure that such placements are fair and accessible.

The main benefit of a compulsory placement is practical experience. Students learn how to apply theory to real problems, work in teams, meet deadlines and communicate professionally, which are skills that lectures rarely teach. They also gain a clearer idea of which careers suit them, so they can choose their future path with more confidence.

Placements also improve employability. Employers often prefer candidates with work experience, and an internship allows students to build a network of contacts and sometimes receive a job offer from the same organisation. For universities, close links with industry can help keep courses relevant to the changing job market.

On the other hand, a requirement for all students could create problems. In some fields, such as theoretical physics or philosophy, suitable placements may be scarce, and unpaid internships disadvantage students from poorer backgrounds who cannot afford to work for free. Therefore, universities should work with employers to offer paid placements, and allow alternatives such as research projects or volunteering where internships are difficult to find.

In conclusion, making work placements a standard part of university education would better prepare graduates for employment, but the policy should be flexible and properly funded so that no student is excluded.

writing.title: Rich countries and climate change
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Wealthy countries should take more responsibility than poorer countries for solving climate change.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: biến đổi khí hậu là vấn đề toàn cầu + quan điểm: đồng ý
Thân 1: lý do lịch sử – nước công nghiệp phát thải phần lớn CO2 tích luỹ, giàu lên nhờ ô nhiễm
Thân 2: có tiền và công nghệ, chia sẻ cho nước đang phát triển; nước nghèo chịu ảnh hưởng nặng nhất
Thân 3 (nhượng bộ): nước đang phát triển cũng phát thải lớn → hợp tác: nước giàu cấp vốn, nước mới nổi phát triển sạch
Kết bài: nước giàu dẫn đầu, mọi nước đóng góp theo khả năng
vocab: Industrialised countries have burned fossil fuels for two centuries.
They should pay more to reduce carbon emissions.
They can invest heavily in renewable energy.
các nền kinh tế mới nổi
Emerging economies must commit to cleaner development.
Wealthy nations should bear most of the burden.
writing.sample:
Climate change is a global problem, but countries differ greatly in how much they have contributed to it and how well they can respond. I agree that wealthy nations should carry a larger share of the responsibility for tackling it.

The most important reason is historical. Industrialised countries have been burning coal, oil and gas for more than two centuries, so they are responsible for most of the carbon dioxide already in the atmosphere. Their prosperity was built partly on this pollution, so it seems fair that they should now pay a greater share of the cost of reducing carbon emissions.

In addition, rich countries have the money and technology to act more quickly. They can invest heavily in renewable energy, electric transport and energy-efficient buildings, and they can share these technologies with developing nations. Poorer countries, by contrast, often struggle to provide basic services such as clean water and electricity, and asking them to sacrifice economic growth would be unrealistic. Ironically, they are frequently the countries most affected by floods, droughts and rising sea levels.

Nevertheless, this does not mean that developing nations have no role to play. Some of them are now among the largest emitters, and their future choices will shape the planet's climate. The best solution is therefore cooperation, with wealthy countries providing finance and expertise while emerging economies commit to cleaner forms of development.

In conclusion, I believe wealthy nations should take the lead and bear most of the burden of fighting climate change, while all countries contribute according to their capacity.

writing.title: Are top athletes paid too much?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Professional athletes are paid far too much money compared with people in other jobs.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: thu nhập khổng lồ của ngôi sao thể thao + quan điểm: đồng ý một phần
Thân 1: khó biện minh so với bác sĩ, giáo viên, y tá; thông điệp lệch lạc cho giới trẻ
Thân 2: lương phản ánh doanh thu khổng lồ (vé, bản quyền, quảng cáo); sự nghiệp ngắn, rủi ro cao
Thân 3: nên tăng lương ngành thiết yếu, khuyến khích đầu tư cho thể thao cộng đồng
Kết bài: quá cao về mặt đạo đức nhưng do thị trường quyết định
vocab: Such salaries seem disproportionate to their social value.
It is hard to defend the gap between athletes and essential workers.
hàng hoá ăn theo (áo, quà lưu niệm)
Stars sell tickets, merchandise and advertising.
Their pay compensates for great risk and sacrifice.
Clubs could invest more in grassroots sport.
writing.sample:
Top footballers, tennis players and basketball stars can earn millions every year, far more than doctors, teachers or nurses. Many people believe this is unjustified. I partly agree: such huge salaries seem disproportionate to their social value, yet they are a natural result of the market.

On the one hand, it is difficult to defend the gap between athletes and essential workers. A surgeon saves lives and a teacher shapes the next generation, while sport, however exciting, is ultimately a form of entertainment. When a single player earns more in a week than a nurse does in several years, it sends a questionable message to young people about what society values.

On the other hand, athletes' earnings reflect the enormous income they generate. Major sporting events attract global television audiences, and clubs and sponsors pay stars because they sell tickets, merchandise and advertising. In addition, professional careers are short, often ending in a player's early thirties, and only a tiny minority of those who train for years ever reach the top. Their pay therefore compensates for great risk and sacrifice.

Rather than limiting what athletes can earn, it would be more effective to address the other side of the problem by improving the pay and conditions of essential workers. Successful sports organisations could also be encouraged to invest more in grassroots sport and community projects.

In conclusion, although the salaries of elite athletes appear excessive in moral terms, they are driven by commercial demand. Society should focus on rewarding vital professions more fairly rather than simply criticising sports stars.

writing.title: Online courses or classroom learning?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Some people think that online courses are just as effective as traditional classroom learning, while others believe that students learn better when they study face to face with a teacher.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: tranh luận học online vs học trực tiếp + quan điểm: học trực tiếp hiệu quả hơn với đa số
Thân 1 (quan điểm A): online tiện, học lại được, chuyên gia giỏi, rẻ/miễn phí
Thân 2 (quan điểm B): tương tác tức thì, phản hồi cá nhân, kỷ luật; tỉ lệ hoàn thành khoá online thấp
Thân 3 (ý kiến riêng): trực tiếp tốt hơn, nhất là học sinh nhỏ; kết hợp blended learning

vocab: The classroom offers advantages that technology cannot replicate.

writing.sample:
The growth of online education has sparked debate about whether learning through a screen can match the experience of a real classroom. While online courses offer impressive flexibility, I believe face-to-face teaching remains more effective for most learners.

Supporters of online learning point to its convenience and accessibility. Students can watch lectures at any time, replay difficult explanations and study from home, which is ideal for working adults or people living far from a university. Online platforms also provide a wide range of courses taught by leading experts, many of them free or inexpensive, so high-quality knowledge is no longer limited to those who can attend elite institutions.

On the other hand, many educators argue that the classroom offers advantages that technology cannot replicate. Learners in a physical classroom benefit from immediate interaction: they can ask questions, take part in discussions and receive personal feedback. The presence of classmates and a fixed timetable also creates motivation and discipline, whereas online students often struggle to stay focused, and completion rates for many online courses are notoriously low.

In my view, traditional teaching is generally superior, particularly for younger students and for subjects that require practical skills or debate. However, the two approaches need not compete. Blended learning, in which students prepare online and then use class time for discussion and problem-solving, combines the flexibility of digital resources with the human contact that keeps learners engaged.

In conclusion, although online courses have made education more accessible, I believe face-to-face learning is still more effective overall, and the best results are likely to come from combining the two.

writing.title: Will AI take jobs or help workers?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: AI lan rộng ở nơi làm việc + quan điểm: cả hai đều xảy ra, tuỳ cách xã hội chuẩn bị

Thân 2 (lạc quan): AI bổ trợ – như bảng tính không xoá nghề kế toán; bác sĩ dùng AI đọc ảnh; nghề mới xuất hiện
Thân 3 (ý kiến): AI xoá một số việc nhưng biến đổi nhiều việc hơn → đào tạo suốt đời
Kết bài: thay thế một số việc, nhưng giúp công việc hiệu quả hơn nếu người lao động được trang bị kỹ năng

writing.sample:
The rapid spread of artificial intelligence in offices and factories has raised concerns about the future of work. Some fear that AI will make millions of workers redundant, while others see it as a tool that will make employees more productive. I believe both outcomes will occur, but the overall effect will depend on how societies manage the transition.

Those who see AI as a threat have good reason for concern. Systems that can write reports, answer customer queries, translate documents and even produce computer code are already performing tasks that once required trained staff. Jobs that consist mainly of routine, predictable work, such as data entry or basic customer service, are particularly vulnerable, and workers in these roles may find it difficult to retrain.

Others argue that AI will mainly complement human workers. Just as spreadsheets did not eliminate accountants, AI tools can take over repetitive tasks and leave people free to focus on creative thinking, decision-making and relationships with clients. Doctors, for example, can use AI to analyse medical images more quickly, allowing them to spend more time with patients. New professions are also likely to emerge, from AI trainers to specialists in data ethics.

In my opinion, AI will eliminate some jobs but transform many more. The real danger is not the technology itself but a lack of preparation. Governments and companies should invest in lifelong training, so that workers can develop the digital and interpersonal skills that machines cannot easily copy.

In conclusion, while AI will undoubtedly replace certain jobs, it can also make work more productive and meaningful, provided that people are given the skills to adapt.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: chi phí khổng lồ của chương trình vũ trụ + quan điểm: vẫn nên đầu tư nhưng ở mức hợp lý
Thân 1 (phản đối): hàng triệu người thiếu nước sạch, y tế, nhà ở; vũ trụ là xa xỉ
Thân 2 (ủng hộ): vệ tinh cho dự báo thời tiết, GPS, theo dõi biến đổi khí hậu; công nghệ ứng dụng; truyền cảm hứng STEM
Thân 3 (ý kiến): không phải chọn một trong hai; ưu tiên nhiệm vụ có giá trị thực tế, hợp tác quốc tế
Kết bài: vấn đề trên Trái Đất ưu tiên, nhưng chương trình vũ trụ được quản lý tốt vẫn đáng đầu tư
vocab: biện minh, chứng minh là hợp lý

writing.sample:
Space programmes cost billions of dollars, and some people question whether this money would be better spent on poverty, healthcare or climate change. Others believe that exploring space is a worthwhile investment. In my opinion, governments should continue to fund space research, but at a level that does not neglect urgent needs at home.

Critics of space spending argue that it is difficult to justify sending missions to Mars while millions of people lack clean water, adequate healthcare or decent housing. The same funds could build hospitals, train teachers or protect communities from floods and droughts. From this perspective, space exploration seems like a luxury that benefits only a small group of scientists and wealthy nations.

However, supporters point out that space research has brought many practical benefits. Satellites provide weather forecasts, GPS navigation and global communications, and they allow scientists to monitor deforestation, melting ice and other effects of climate change. Technologies first developed for space, such as water purification systems and improved medical imaging, are now used in everyday life. Space exploration also inspires young people to study science and engineering, which strengthens a country's economy in the long run.

I believe these arguments show that the choice is not simply between space and Earth, since much space research directly helps us understand and protect our own planet. Nevertheless, governments should prioritise missions with clear scientific or practical value and cooperate with other countries to share costs, rather than competing for national prestige.

In conclusion, while problems on Earth must remain the priority, a carefully managed space programme is a valuable investment whose benefits extend far beyond outer space.

writing.title: Who should teach children good behaviour?
writing.prompt:

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: hành vi của trẻ chịu nhiều ảnh hưởng + quan điểm: cha mẹ chịu trách nhiệm chính
Thân 1 (cha mẹ): tính cách hình thành sớm, trẻ bắt chước người lớn, cha mẹ hiểu con và kèm cặp lâu dài
Thân 2 (nhà trường): giáo viên chuyên nghiệp, công bằng; trẻ học chia sẻ, hợp tác; bù đắp cho gia đình khó khăn
Thân 3 (ý kiến): trường củng cố nhưng không thay thế gia đình; hợp tác cha mẹ – giáo viên
Kết bài: cha mẹ là chính, trường hỗ trợ
vocab: Parents' behaviour becomes a model for their children.
Schools can compensate for difficult home environments.

writing.sample:
Children's behaviour is shaped by many influences, and there is disagreement about who should play the main role in teaching good manners and values. While schools make an important contribution, I believe parents bear the primary responsibility.

Those who emphasise the role of parents argue that a child's character is formed long before they start school. In the first years of life, children learn by copying the adults around them, so the way parents speak, resolve conflicts and treat others becomes a model for their own behaviour. Parents also know their children best and can guide them consistently over many years, rewarding kindness and correcting rudeness in everyday situations.

Others believe schools are better placed to teach behaviour. Teachers are trained professionals who can explain rules clearly and treat all pupils equally. At school, children must share, take turns and cooperate with classmates from different backgrounds, which teaches social skills that are difficult to learn at home. In addition, some parents are too busy or lack the knowledge to teach these values, so schools can compensate for difficult home environments.

In my view, schools should reinforce good behaviour, but they cannot replace the influence of the family. A teacher responsible for thirty children has limited time with each of them, and lessons about respect will have little effect if they contradict what a child sees at home. The ideal situation is a partnership in which parents and teachers communicate regularly and share the same expectations.

In conclusion, although schools play a valuable supporting role, parents should take the main responsibility for teaching children to behave well, since their example has the deepest and most lasting impact.

writing.title: Tourism: economic gain or cultural loss?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Some people say that international tourism brings economic benefits to local communities, while others argue that it damages their culture and environment.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: du lịch quốc tế bùng nổ + quan điểm: có lợi nếu được quản lý tốt
Thân 1 (lợi ích kinh tế): việc làm, thu nhập, thuế cho hạ tầng, ngoại tệ
Thân 2 (tác hại): quá tải, giá nhà tăng đẩy người dân đi, văn hoá bị thương mại hoá, môi trường bị phá
Thân 3 (ý kiến): giới hạn lượng khách, thuế du lịch cho bảo tồn, du lịch cộng đồng, du khách có trách nhiệm
Kết bài: lợi ích kinh tế đáng kể; cần quản lý và trao quyền cho cộng đồng
vocab: Tourism is one of the main sources of foreign currency.
Holiday rentals push up property prices.

writing.sample:
International tourism has grown enormously over recent decades, transforming many towns and villages. Some see this as a valuable source of income for local people, while others believe it threatens their culture and natural surroundings. I think tourism can be beneficial overall, but only if it is carefully managed.

The economic case for tourism is strong. Visitors spend money on hotels, restaurants, transport and souvenirs, creating jobs for local residents, including in remote areas with few other industries. Tax revenue from tourism can also pay for better roads, airports and public services. In many developing countries, tourism is one of the main sources of foreign currency.

However, critics highlight the hidden costs. Popular destinations can become overcrowded, and rising demand for holiday rentals often pushes up property prices, forcing local people to move away. Traditional festivals and crafts may be turned into commercial performances for tourists, losing their original meaning. The environment also suffers from increased waste, heavy water consumption and damage to fragile sites such as coral reefs and historic buildings.

In my opinion, these problems are real but avoidable. Authorities can limit visitor numbers at sensitive sites, introduce tourist taxes to fund conservation, and encourage community-based tourism, in which local people own businesses and decide how their culture is presented. Visitors themselves can choose responsible operators and respect local customs.

In conclusion, while international tourism can harm local culture and the environment, its economic benefits are significant. With sensible regulation and greater local control, tourism can support communities rather than damage them.

Thân 2 (ủng hộ): văn hoá là lợi ích công, giữ bản sắc, gắn kết cộng đồng; nghệ thuật truyền thống cần hỗ trợ; tạo việc làm, du lịch
Thân 3 (ý kiến): dịch vụ thiết yếu trước, nhưng chi phí cho nghệ thuật rất nhỏ; tập trung giúp nhiều người tiếp cận
Kết bài: ưu tiên y tế, giáo dục nhưng vẫn hỗ trợ nghệ thuật

Governments have limited budgets, so decisions about public spending often involve difficult choices. Some argue that the arts deserve state funding, while others believe every available dollar should go to essential services such as hospitals and schools. In my view, the arts should receive a modest but secure share of public money.

Those who oppose arts funding argue that healthcare and education meet basic needs and affect everyone's quality of life. When hospitals have long waiting lists and schools lack teachers, spending money on opera houses or art exhibitions can seem irresponsible. They also argue that popular forms of entertainment can survive commercially, so public subsidies mainly benefit wealthier audiences.

On the other hand, supporters of the arts believe culture is also a public good. Music, theatre and visual art help a nation preserve its identity, bring communities together and give young people opportunities to develop their creativity. Many artistic activities, such as local theatre groups or traditional music, would disappear without public support because they do not generate enough profit. Moreover, the cultural sector creates jobs and attracts tourists, so funding it can bring economic returns.

I believe that essential services must come first, but the arts are not a luxury. The amount needed to support them is usually very small compared with health or education budgets, while the social benefits can be considerable. Public funding should, however, focus on making the arts accessible, for example through cheap tickets, school programmes and community projects.

In conclusion, although healthcare and education should remain the priority, governments should continue to support the arts because they enrich society in ways that markets alone cannot.

writing.title: A fixed retirement age?

Thân 2 (làm tiếp): kinh nghiệm, kèm cặp; dân số già, chi phí lương hưu; công việc mang lại thu nhập, mục đích, sức khoẻ
Thân 3 (ý kiến): 'người già chiếm việc của người trẻ' là ngộ nhận; làm bán thời gian, nghỉ hưu dần; đánh giá theo năng lực

writing.sample:
As people live longer and healthier lives, the question of when they should stop working has become increasingly important. Some believe a fixed retirement age is necessary to make room for younger workers, while others think older employees should decide for themselves. I support the second view, as long as workplaces adapt to changing abilities.

The argument for a fixed retirement age is mainly about fairness between generations. In many countries youth unemployment is high, and when senior staff remain in their posts for decades, promotion opportunities for younger colleagues become scarce. A clear retirement age also allows organisations to plan ahead and bring fresh ideas into leadership roles.

However, forcing capable people to stop working can be wasteful and unjust. Older employees often have valuable experience, professional networks and judgement that take years to develop, and they can mentor younger colleagues. Moreover, with ageing populations and rising pension costs, many economies actually need people to work longer. For individuals, work can provide income, purpose and social contact, all of which are important for mental and physical health.

In my opinion, the idea that older workers take jobs away from the young is largely a myth, since the number of jobs in an economy is not fixed. Rather than imposing a compulsory retirement age, governments should offer flexible options such as part-time work or gradual retirement, and employers should judge people on their performance rather than their age.

In conclusion, although a fixed retirement age may seem to help young people, I believe older workers should be free to continue working, provided they remain able to perform their roles effectively.

Where children grow up can influence their health, education and opportunities. Some parents prefer the energy and facilities of a big city, while others value the space and calm of the countryside. Although both environments have advantages, I believe the countryside generally offers a better childhood.

Supporters of city life point to the range of opportunities available. Cities usually have better-funded schools, libraries and museums, as well as clubs for almost every sport or hobby. Children growing up in a diverse urban environment also meet people from different cultures, which can make them more open-minded and confident. In addition, good public transport allows teenagers to travel independently.

On the other hand, the countryside offers a healthier and safer environment. Clean air, open spaces and contact with nature encourage children to play outdoors and stay physically active instead of spending hours on screens. Rural villages also tend to be close-knit communities where neighbours know one another, so children can enjoy more freedom without the dangers of heavy traffic. Many psychologists believe that time in nature reduces stress and improves concentration.

In my view, these benefits are especially important during the early years of childhood, when health, play and a sense of security matter more than access to museums or shopping centres. The main drawback of rural life, the lack of educational and cultural facilities, can be partly overcome through online learning and occasional trips to the city.

In conclusion, while cities provide valuable opportunities, I believe the countryside is a better place for most children to grow up, especially when they are young.

Thân 2 (cá nhân): hàng triệu người cùng thay đổi tạo tác động lớn; nhu cầu tiêu dùng thay đổi thị trường; cử tri gây áp lực

Kết bài: cần hành động mạnh của chính phủ, cá nhân góp phần qua lựa chọn và áp lực

Problems such as climate change, plastic pollution and the loss of wildlife affect the whole planet. Some people believe only governments have the power to address them, while others argue that individual actions matter. In my opinion, government action is essential, but personal choices also play an important role.

Those who emphasise the role of governments argue that the scale of environmental damage is too great for individuals. A single person recycling bottles or switching off lights has a tiny impact compared with the emissions of power stations, factories and transport networks. Only governments can pass laws on pollution, invest in renewable energy, protect forests and negotiate international agreements. Without such policies, individual efforts can feel meaningless.

On the other hand, many people believe that change begins with individuals. When millions of consumers reduce waste, eat less meat or choose public transport, the combined effect can be considerable. Consumer demand also influences businesses: the growing popularity of reusable bags and electric cars shows how personal choices can change entire markets. Moreover, governments in democracies respond to public opinion, so people who care about the environment are more likely to vote for leaders who take it seriously.

I believe the two approaches depend on each other. Governments must create the conditions that make environmentally friendly choices easy and affordable, for instance by improving recycling systems and public transport. At the same time, individuals need to support these policies and adjust their habits, otherwise even the best laws will have limited effect.

In conclusion, environmental problems require strong government action, but individuals still have an important part to play, both through their daily choices and through the pressure they put on decision-makers.

With rising levels of obesity and diet-related illness, many people have called for restrictions on the advertising of unhealthy food. Others argue that such bans interfere with personal freedom. Supporters of a ban argue that advertising is designed to influence choices, often in ways that people do not notice. Fast-food and snack companies spend huge sums on colourful adverts, celebrity endorsements and online promotions that make high-fat, high-sugar products appear fun and desirable. Children are especially vulnerable, as they cannot easily recognise persuasive techniques, and eating habits formed in childhood often last a lifetime.

Opponents believe that a ban would treat adults like children. They argue that people have the right to decide what they eat, and that the solution to unhealthy diets lies in education rather than censorship. Food companies are legal businesses, and restricting their advertising could damage the economy, particularly the media outlets that depend on advertising revenue. Furthermore, it is difficult to define exactly which foods are unhealthy, since most can be eaten safely in moderation.

I believe both arguments have merit, but the case for protecting children is particularly strong. Advertising for unhealthy products should be banned during children's programmes, on websites popular with young people and near schools. For adults, clear nutritional labelling and public health campaigns are a fairer way to encourage better choices without removing freedom.

In conclusion, although adults should be able to choose their own food, restricting unhealthy food advertising aimed at children is a reasonable step to protect public health.

writing.title: Working from home
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many companies, employees are now allowed to work from home for some or all of the week.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: làm việc từ xa phổ biến sau đại dịch + quan điểm: lợi ích lớn hơn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): bỏ thời gian/chi phí đi lại; linh hoạt cho cha mẹ, người chăm sóc; công ty giảm chi phí văn phòng, tuyển người ở xa
Thân 2 (bất lợi): cô lập; nhân viên trẻ thiếu học hỏi; giao tiếp chậm; ranh giới công việc – đời sống bị xoá nhoà
Thân 3 (đánh giá): mô hình hybrid, quy định giờ làm → bất lợi khắc phục được
Kết bài: lợi ích lớn hơn, nhất là khi kết hợp vài ngày lên văn phòng
vocab: đi lại giữa nhà và nơi làm
Remote workers no longer need to commute every day.
sức khoẻ thể chất và tinh thần
Avoiding long journeys improves employees' well-being.
Working from home can be isolating.
Remote work can blur the boundary between work and private life.
mô hình làm việc kết hợp (văn phòng + tại nhà)
tình trạng kiệt sức vì công việc
Clear rules on working hours protect staff from burnout.
writing.sample:
Since the pandemic, a growing number of companies have allowed staff to work from home for part or all of the week. Although remote working has certain drawbacks, I believe its advantages are greater for both employees and employers.

The most obvious benefit for workers is the time and money saved by not commuting. Instead of spending hours in traffic or on crowded trains, employees can use this time to rest, exercise or be with their families, which often improves their well-being and productivity. Remote work also gives people more flexibility to organise their day, making it easier for parents and carers to combine a career with responsibilities at home. For employers, it reduces the cost of office space and allows them to recruit talented staff who live far from the company's headquarters.

On the other hand, working from home can be isolating. Without daily contact with colleagues, some employees feel less connected to their organisation, and younger staff in particular may miss out on the informal learning that comes from watching experienced colleagues. Communication can also become slower, as quick conversations in the corridor are replaced by emails and scheduled video calls. Furthermore, the boundary between work and private life can become blurred, leading some people to work longer hours than before.

In my view, these problems can largely be solved through sensible arrangements. Hybrid models, in which employees spend two or three days a week in the office, preserve face-to-face collaboration while keeping most of the benefits of flexibility, and clear rules about working hours can protect staff from burnout.

In conclusion, although remote working can reduce social contact and blur the line between work and home, its benefits in terms of time, flexibility and cost outweigh these disadvantages.

writing.title: Young children with their own devices
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: trẻ nhỏ có điện thoại/máy tính bảng riêng + quan điểm: bất lợi lớn hơn, nhất là với trẻ rất nhỏ
Thân 1 (lợi ích): kỹ năng số, ứng dụng học tập, gọi video với người thân, cha mẹ yên tâm liên lạc
Thân 2 (bất lợi): ít chơi ngoài trời, đọc sách, trò chuyện; ngủ kém, kém tập trung; rủi ro trên mạng; ứng dụng gây nghiện
Thân 3 (đánh giá): dùng máy chung của gia đình, giới hạn thời gian, có người lớn giám sát; điện thoại riêng khi lớn hơn
Kết bài: bất lợi lớn hơn khi trẻ có thiết bị riêng quá sớm
vocab: A phone gives parents peace of mind.
thời gian dùng màn hình quá mức

Online bullying is a serious risk for children.
Many apps are deliberately designed to be addictive.
dưới sự giám sát của người lớn
Children should use tablets under adult supervision.
writing.sample:
It is increasingly common to see young children using their own smartphones or tablets, sometimes even before they start school. While these devices offer some benefits, I believe the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, particularly for very young children.

Supporters of early access to technology argue that it helps children develop the digital skills they will need in the future. Educational apps can teach reading, numbers and foreign languages in an entertaining way, and video calls allow children to stay in touch with relatives who live far away. Parents also say that a phone gives them peace of mind, since they can contact their child at any time.

However, the risks are considerable. Young children who spend hours on screens have less time for activities that are essential to their development, such as playing outside, reading books and talking face to face with family and friends. Excessive screen time has been linked to poor sleep, weaker concentration and a lack of physical activity. Moreover, children are not mature enough to deal with the dangers of the internet, including inappropriate content, online bullying and contact with strangers. Many apps are also deliberately designed to be addictive, which makes it very hard for young users to put their devices down.

In my opinion, the educational benefits of these devices can be gained without giving a child unlimited personal access. Sharing a family tablet for short periods, under adult supervision, allows children to learn from technology while protecting them from its harms. A personal smartphone is more appropriate when children are older and more responsible.

In conclusion, although smartphones and tablets can support learning and communication, their negative effects on children's health, development and safety outweigh these benefits when devices are given at a very young age.

writing.title: Going abroad to study
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

An increasing number of students choose to go to another country to study at university.

What are the advantages and disadvantages of this?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: ngày càng nhiều sinh viên du học + nêu sẽ bàn cả lợi ích và khó khăn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): giáo dục chất lượng cao, bằng cấp uy tín; ngoại ngữ tiến bộ nhanh; độc lập, thích nghi, cởi mở
Thân 2 (bất lợi): học phí, chi phí sinh hoạt cao; sốc văn hoá, nhớ nhà; chảy máu chất xám
Kết bài: trải nghiệm thay đổi cuộc đời nhưng cần cân nhắc tài chính và tinh thần; nhà nước nên có học bổng, việc làm hấp dẫn để thu hút người về
vocab: A foreign degree can improve graduates' career prospects.
Students abroad become more independent and adaptable.
Living expenses can be a heavy burden for families.
Many students experience culture shock in their first year.
Homesickness is common among international students.

writing.sample:
Every year, more young people leave their home countries to attend universities abroad. This trend offers students valuable opportunities, but it also brings significant challenges.

The main advantage of studying abroad is access to high-quality education. Many leading universities offer courses, research facilities and teaching methods that are not available in students' home countries, and a degree from a respected foreign institution can improve graduates' career prospects. In addition, living in another country is an education in itself. Students improve their language skills far more quickly than they would in a classroom at home, and by meeting people from many cultures they become more independent, adaptable and open-minded, qualities that international employers value highly.

However, there are also clear disadvantages. The most serious is cost: tuition fees for international students are often much higher than for local students, and living expenses in cities such as London or Sydney can be a heavy burden for families. Many students also experience culture shock and homesickness, especially in their first year, when they must cope with an unfamiliar language, climate and academic system without the support of family and friends. Finally, some graduates decide not to return home, which can contribute to a brain drain in which developing countries lose many of their most talented young people.

Overall, studying abroad can be a life-changing experience that broadens both academic and personal horizons. Nevertheless, students should consider the financial and emotional challenges carefully, and governments could do more, through scholarships and attractive jobs at home, to ensure that their countries also share in the benefits.

writing.title: Tourism in remote natural areas
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Tourists are increasingly travelling to remote natural areas, such as rainforests, deserts and the polar regions.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: du lịch đến vùng hoang sơ (Amazon, Nam Cực) tăng + quan điểm: bất lợi lớn hơn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): phí tham quan nuôi vườn quốc gia, dự án bảo tồn; thu nhập cho cộng đồng bản địa; nâng cao nhận thức môi trường
Thân 2 (bất lợi): hệ sinh thái mong manh, phục hồi chậm; xây khách sạn, đường, sân bay phá môi trường sống; bay đường dài tăng khí thải; văn hoá bản địa bị xáo trộn
Thân 3 (đề xuất): giới hạn số khách, bắt buộc đi cùng hướng dẫn viên được cấp phép, dùng tiền thu được cho bảo tồn
Kết bài: tác hại lớn hơn lợi ích nếu không kiểm soát chặt
vocab: Tourism provides income for indigenous communities.
Cruises produce large amounts of carbon emissions.
giới hạn số lượng du khách
writing.sample:
Holidays in places that were once almost impossible to reach, such as the Amazon rainforest or Antarctica, have become increasingly popular. Although this kind of tourism can bring some benefits, I believe its disadvantages are greater.

Admittedly, visiting remote natural areas can have positive effects. Entrance fees and tourist spending can help to fund national parks and conservation projects, and they provide income for local and indigenous communities who might otherwise depend on logging or mining. Furthermore, people who see endangered animals or melting glaciers with their own eyes often return home with a deeper understanding of environmental problems and a stronger commitment to protecting nature.

However, these advantages are outweighed by the damage that tourism can cause to fragile ecosystems. Such areas often recover very slowly, so even small amounts of litter, noise or trampling can have lasting effects on plants and wildlife. Building hotels, roads and airports to serve visitors destroys natural habitats and opens untouched areas to further development. In addition, reaching these distant places usually requires long-haul flights or cruises, which produce large amounts of carbon emissions and therefore contribute to the very climate change that threatens these environments. The sudden arrival of large numbers of outsiders can also disrupt the traditional way of life of indigenous groups.

For these reasons, tourism in remote natural areas should be strictly limited. Governments could cap visitor numbers, require tourists to travel with licensed guides and invest the income directly in conservation and local communities.

In conclusion, although tourism in remote regions can raise money and awareness, its harmful effects on fragile environments and local cultures outweigh these benefits unless it is carefully controlled.

writing.title: A cashless society
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In some countries, cash is rapidly being replaced by electronic payments, such as bank cards and mobile phone apps.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: thanh toán điện tử thay thế tiền mặt + quan điểm: lợi ích lớn hơn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): nhanh, tiện; giao dịch được lưu lại → quản lý chi tiêu, chống trốn thuế, rửa tiền; doanh nghiệp giảm chi phí và nguy cơ bị cướp
Thân 2 (bất lợi): người già, người khuyết tật, thu nhập thấp bị gạt ra ngoài; lỗi hệ thống, tấn công mạng; quyền riêng tư
Thân 3 (giải pháp): bắt buộc nhận tiền mặt cho hàng thiết yếu, hỗ trợ mở tài khoản, luật bảo vệ dữ liệu
Kết bài: lợi ích lớn hơn, miễn là tiền mặt vẫn còn cho người cần
vocab: Digital records make it easier to detect tax evasion.
Electronic payments help governments fight money laundering.
Older people risk being excluded from everyday services.
Payment systems are vulnerable to cyberattacks.
People may be unable to buy basic necessities.
Governments should enforce strict rules on data protection.
writing.sample:
In many countries, people now pay for almost everything with bank cards or mobile phone apps, and some shops no longer accept cash at all. Although a cashless society raises some concerns, I believe its advantages are greater.

The most obvious benefit is convenience. Electronic payments are fast, and people no longer need to carry coins and notes or look for cash machines. Digital transactions also leave a record, which makes it easier for individuals to track their spending and for governments to detect tax evasion, money laundering and other financial crimes. Businesses benefit too, as they save the time and cost of counting, storing and transporting cash, and they face a lower risk of robbery.

However, the disappearance of cash also has disadvantages. Older people, those with disabilities and people on low incomes may lack smartphones, bank accounts or the necessary digital skills, so they risk being excluded from everyday services. Electronic systems are also vulnerable to technical failures and cyberattacks; when a payment network goes down, people may be unable to buy even basic necessities. In addition, every digital payment can be recorded, which raises concerns about privacy and the amount of personal information held by banks and technology companies.

In my view, these problems are serious but manageable. Governments can require shops to keep accepting cash for essential goods, help vulnerable groups to open basic bank accounts and enforce strict rules on data protection and cybersecurity.

In conclusion, although a cashless society may exclude some people and create new risks to privacy and security, its convenience, efficiency and ability to reduce crime outweigh these drawbacks, as long as cash remains available for those who need it.

writing.title: More people living alone
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.

Living alone helps young adults become self-reliant.
vấn đề sức khoẻ cộng đồng

writing.sample:
In many countries, the number of one-person households has risen sharply, as people marry later, divorce more often and live longer. While living alone offers certain benefits, I believe its disadvantages, both for individuals and for society, are more significant.

For many people, living alone represents freedom and independence. They can organise their homes and daily routines exactly as they wish, without having to compromise with partners or flatmates. Young adults who live alone also learn to manage money, cook and solve problems for themselves, which helps them become more mature and self-reliant. For some, a private space is also important for rest, concentration and creativity.

However, living alone has considerable drawbacks. The most serious is loneliness, which is now recognised as a public health issue and can lead to depression and other illnesses, especially among elderly people who have lost a partner. People who live alone may also have nobody to help them in an emergency, such as a fall or a sudden illness. Financially, a single person must pay the full cost of rent, energy bills and household goods, which is far more expensive than sharing. At the level of society, the trend increases demand for housing, pushing up prices and leading to the construction of more homes, which uses more land and energy.

These problems call for action. Cities could encourage shared housing such as co-living buildings with communal kitchens, and local communities should offer activities and support networks for older residents living on their own.

In conclusion, although living alone gives people independence and privacy, its negative effects on well-being, personal finances and the housing supply outweigh these advantages.

writing.title: Food from around the world all year round
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Today, supermarkets in many countries sell food produced all over the world, so people can buy fruit and vegetables from other countries at any time of year.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: siêu thị bán thực phẩm khắp thế giới quanh năm + quan điểm: lợi ích lớn hơn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): lựa chọn đa dạng, ăn uống cân bằng quanh năm; quan trọng ở nơi khí hậu khắc nghiệt; giá rẻ hơn; thu nhập cho nông dân ở nước đang phát triển
Thân 2 (bất lợi): vận chuyển xa → khí thải, bao bì, làm lạnh; nông dân địa phương khó cạnh tranh; mất hương vị, mất thói quen ăn theo mùa
Thân 3 (đánh giá): phần lớn hàng đi đường biển, khí thải thấp hơn; dán nhãn rõ để người mua chọn hàng địa phương, theo mùa
Kết bài: lợi ích về đa dạng, giá cả, dinh dưỡng lớn hơn

writing.sample:
Thanks to global trade, supermarket shelves in many countries are filled with produce from around the world, so shoppers can buy strawberries in winter or tropical fruit in cold climates. Although this has some negative effects, I believe the advantages are greater.

The main benefit is choice. Consumers can enjoy a varied and balanced diet throughout the year, rather than relying on the limited range of food that grows locally in each season. This is particularly important in countries with harsh climates, where few fresh fruits and vegetables can be grown in winter. Imported food can also be cheaper, since it is produced where conditions are ideal. Moreover, international trade provides income for farmers in developing countries, many of whom depend on exports of products such as coffee, bananas and avocados.

On the other hand, transporting food over long distances has environmental costs. Air-freighted produce, in particular, generates significant carbon emissions, and large amounts of packaging and refrigeration are needed to keep food fresh. Local farmers may also struggle to compete with cheap imports, which can threaten rural jobs and traditional agriculture. Some people also argue that food picked before it is ripe and transported for days loses its flavour, and that people are losing touch with the natural seasons.

Nevertheless, these problems can be reduced without giving up the benefits. Most imported food travels by sea, which produces far lower emissions than air freight, and clear labelling would allow consumers to choose local and seasonal products when they are available.

In conclusion, while year-round access to food from all over the world has environmental and economic drawbacks, the benefits of variety, affordability and better nutrition outweigh them.

writing.title: Shopping centres replacing local shops
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many towns and cities, large shopping centres are replacing small local shops.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: trung tâm thương mại lớn thay thế cửa hàng nhỏ + quan điểm: bất lợi lớn hơn

Thân 2 (bất lợi): mất bản sắc khu phố và sự gắn kết; phố vắng, kém an toàn; lợi nhuận chảy khỏi địa phương; khuyến khích lái xe → ô nhiễm; khó cho người già không có xe

Kết bài: bất lợi lớn hơn lợi ích

writing.sample:
In many towns, small family-run shops are closing as large shopping centres open on the outskirts or in city centres. Although shopping centres offer convenience, I believe the disadvantages of this trend outweigh the advantages.

There are certainly reasons why shopping centres are popular. They bring a wide range of stores, restaurants and entertainment together under one roof, allowing customers to buy everything they need in a single trip. Because large retailers buy in bulk, their prices are often lower than those of independent shops. Shopping centres are also comfortable in all weathers, provide plenty of parking and create many jobs.

However, the loss of local shops has serious consequences for communities. Small businesses give each neighbourhood its own character, and their owners often know their customers personally, which creates a sense of community that is hard to find in a chain store. When these shops disappear, high streets can become empty, unattractive and even unsafe. Profits made by national or international chains also tend to leave the area, whereas money spent in independent shops is more likely to stay in the local economy. Furthermore, out-of-town shopping centres encourage people to drive, which increases traffic and pollution, and they make life harder for elderly people and others without cars.

To protect local shops, councils could reduce taxes for small retailers, limit the construction of new out-of-town centres and organise markets and events that bring people back to the high street.

In conclusion, while shopping centres offer choice and convenience, the damage they cause to local economies, community life and the environment means that their disadvantages outweigh their advantages.

writing.title: Replacing petrol cars with electric vehicles
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Many governments plan to ban the sale of new petrol and diesel cars and replace them with electric vehicles.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: chính phủ cấm bán xe xăng/dầu mới + quan điểm: lợi ích lớn hơn
Thân 1 (lợi ích): không khí sạch, giảm bệnh hô hấp; giảm khí thải nếu điện từ năng lượng tái tạo; êm, chi phí vận hành và bảo dưỡng thấp
Thân 2 (bất lợi): giá mua cao; thiếu trạm sạc; khai thác lithium, cobalt gây hại môi trường, điều kiện lao động kém; mất việc trong ngành động cơ truyền thống
Thân 3 (đánh giá): phần lớn là vấn đề tạm thời – giá pin giảm, trợ giá, mạng lưới sạc, tái chế pin, đào tạo lại lao động
Kết bài: lợi ích lâu dài cho sức khoẻ và khí hậu lớn hơn
vocab: Electric cars produce no exhaust fumes.
Electric vehicles help countries meet their climate targets.
Many countries lack enough charging points.
The extraction of lithium can damage the environment.
Governments can provide subsidies for buyers.
writing.sample:
Several governments have announced plans to end the sale of new petrol and diesel cars and encourage drivers to switch to electric vehicles. Although this policy creates some difficulties, I believe its advantages outweigh them.

The greatest benefit is cleaner air. Electric cars produce no exhaust fumes, so replacing petrol and diesel vehicles would significantly reduce the air pollution that causes respiratory diseases in busy cities. If the electricity comes from renewable sources such as solar and wind power, electric vehicles also produce far lower carbon emissions over their lifetime, helping countries to meet their climate targets. In addition, electric cars are quieter and usually cheaper to run and maintain, since electricity costs less than fuel and electric motors have fewer moving parts.

However, the transition presents real challenges. Electric cars are still more expensive to buy than conventional models, which may make them unaffordable for low-income families. Many countries also lack enough charging points, especially in rural areas and in apartment buildings without private parking. Moreover, batteries require minerals such as lithium and cobalt, whose extraction can damage the environment and is sometimes linked to poor working conditions. Finally, workers in factories that make traditional engines may lose their jobs.

In my view, most of these problems are temporary and can be addressed. Battery prices have fallen considerably in recent years, and governments can provide subsidies, invest in charging networks, and support battery recycling and retraining programmes for affected workers.

In conclusion, although moving to electric vehicles involves high costs and practical obstacles, the long-term benefits for public health and the climate outweigh these disadvantages.

Countries often spend years competing for the right to host major sporting events such as the Olympic Games or the football World Cup. Hosting these events can bring considerable benefits, but it also involves significant costs and risks.

One of the main advantages is the boost to a country's international image. Millions of people around the world watch the event, which can attract tourists and foreign investment for years afterwards. Hosting also creates an opportunity to improve infrastructure: new railway lines, airports and sports facilities built for the event can continue to serve local people long after it ends. In addition, a major tournament can generate national pride and inspire young people to take up sport and lead healthier lives.

On the other hand, the financial costs are enormous. Building stadiums, athletes' villages and security systems can cost billions, and the final bill is often far higher than originally planned. Some venues are rarely used once the event is over, leaving expensive buildings that become a burden on public budgets, while the same money might have been spent on schools, hospitals or housing. Furthermore, construction can force residents to leave their homes, and huge numbers of visitors can lead to overcrowding, rising prices and environmental damage.

Overall, whether hosting is beneficial depends largely on careful planning. Countries that reuse existing venues, design new facilities for long-term community use and keep budgets under control are far more likely to enjoy lasting benefits than those that build for a few weeks of global attention.

In conclusion, hosting international sporting events can enhance a nation's reputation, infrastructure and morale, but these benefits come with heavy financial, social and environmental costs that must be carefully managed.

In many major cities, the cost of buying or renting a home has risen far faster than incomes, leaving many young people unable to afford a place of their own. This problem has several causes, but there are also practical steps that governments could take to address it.

As jobs and universities are concentrated in large cities, more and more people move there, yet the construction of new homes has not kept pace, partly because land is scarce and planning procedures are slow. Several measures could improve the situation. Firstly, governments should increase the supply of affordable homes, both by building social housing directly and by simplifying planning rules so that developers can build more quickly, particularly near public transport. Secondly, taxes on empty properties and on people who own multiple homes would discourage speculation and release more housing onto the market. Thirdly, first-time buyers could receive help through low-interest loans or shared-ownership schemes, in which they buy part of a property and rent the rest. In conclusion, the housing crisis in big cities is caused by high demand, limited supply and property speculation, but it can be eased through more construction, fairer taxation and targeted support for young buyers.
