Many people today complain that their jobs leave them little time or energy for family, friends and rest, and work-related stress has become extremely common. This essay will examine the main causes of this problem and suggest some possible solutions.

One major cause is the rise of digital technology. Because smartphones and laptops allow employees to read emails and messages anywhere, many feel they are expected to be available outside working hours, so work gradually spreads into evenings, weekends and even holidays. Another cause is economic pressure. In competitive industries, workers often stay late or take on extra tasks because they fear losing their jobs or missing out on promotion, while rising living costs force some people to take a second job. Long commutes in large cities also reduce the time available for rest and family life.

There are several ways to tackle this problem. Employers have an important role to play: they can set clear rules about contacting staff outside working hours, as some countries have done through 'right to disconnect' laws, and offer flexible schedules or remote work so that employees can manage family responsibilities more easily. Managers should also be trained to recognise signs of stress and to set realistic workloads. Individuals, for their part, can protect their personal time by switching off work notifications in the evening and planning regular exercise and social activities. Governments could support these efforts by enforcing limits on working hours and investing in public transport to shorten commutes.

In conclusion, the difficulty of balancing work and private life results mainly from constant connectivity, job insecurity and long commutes. A combination of responsible employers, sensible personal habits and supportive government policies can help people lead healthier and more balanced lives.

Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic waste find their way into the world's oceans, where they harm marine life and break down into tiny particles that enter the food chain. This essay will discuss the main causes of this problem and suggest some solutions.

The root cause is the enormous amount of plastic that modern societies use, much of it only once. Products such as bottles, bags, food containers and packaging are cheap and convenient, so they are used in huge quantities and quickly thrown away. A second cause is poor waste management. In many countries, especially fast-growing ones, rubbish collection and recycling systems cannot cope with the volume of waste, so plastic is dumped in open landfills or rivers, which carry it to the sea. Fishing is another source, as lost or abandoned nets and lines make up a large share of the plastic floating in the ocean.

Tackling this problem requires action at several levels. Firstly, governments should reduce the use of single-use plastics by banning or taxing items such as plastic bags, straws and disposable cutlery, and by encouraging reusable alternatives. Secondly, manufacturers should be made responsible for the packaging they produce, which would encourage them to design products that are easier to recycle. Thirdly, wealthy countries could provide funding and expertise to help developing nations build effective waste collection and recycling systems. Finally, the fishing industry should be required to mark and recover its equipment.

In conclusion, ocean plastic pollution results from excessive consumption of disposable plastic, inadequate waste management and fishing waste. Reducing plastic use, making producers responsible and improving waste systems around the world would go a long way towards cleaning up our seas.

Traffic jams have become a daily feature of life in many cities, wasting time, polluting the air and raising stress levels. There are several reasons for this situation, but it can be improved through a combination of measures.

The most fundamental cause is rapid urbanisation. As more people move to cities for work and education, the number of journeys rises, but road space cannot expand at the same rate. Rising incomes have also enabled millions of households to buy cars or motorbikes for the first time, and many people regard private vehicles as more comfortable and reliable than public transport, which in some cities is slow, crowded or poorly connected. In addition, poor urban planning often separates homes from workplaces, schools and shops, so residents must travel long distances every day, usually at the same peak times.

To reduce congestion, governments should first invest in fast, frequent and affordable public transport, such as metro lines and bus rapid transit systems, so that leaving the car at home becomes an attractive choice. Secondly, charging drivers to enter busy central areas at peak times, as London and Singapore have done, can discourage unnecessary journeys and raise money for public transport. Thirdly, planners should design mixed-use neighbourhoods, where people can live close to their work and daily needs, and provide safe routes for walking and cycling. Finally, employers could help by allowing flexible working hours or remote work, which spreads journeys more evenly throughout the day.

In conclusion, traffic congestion is caused by urban growth, rising car ownership and poor planning. Better public transport, road pricing, smarter urban design and flexible working could make city streets far less crowded.

In many countries, young people leaving school or university face great difficulty finding work, and youth unemployment rates are often far higher than those for older adults. This essay will examine why this happens and how the problem might be addressed.

One important reason is the gap between what young people learn and what employers need. Many education systems still focus on theoretical knowledge and exam results, so graduates often lack practical skills such as communication, teamwork and the ability to use specialist software. A second reason is lack of experience. Employers tend to prefer candidates who have already worked, which traps young people in a cycle in which they cannot get a job without experience and cannot gain experience without a job. In addition, in some countries the number of graduates has grown faster than the number of professional jobs, while technological change is reducing the number of entry-level positions in offices and factories.

Several measures could help. Firstly, schools and universities should work more closely with businesses to keep courses up to date and to include practical projects, internships and career guidance. Secondly, governments could offer tax incentives to companies that hire and train young people, for example through apprenticeship schemes that combine paid work with study. Thirdly, vocational education should be given greater status, so that more students choose training in fields such as healthcare, technology and skilled trades, where demand for workers is high. Finally, support for young entrepreneurs, including small loans and business advice, would allow some to create their own jobs.

In conclusion, youth unemployment results from a mismatch of skills, a lack of experience and changes in the labour market. Closer cooperation between education and industry, incentives for employers and better vocational training could give young people a much better start in working life.

In several countries, there is growing concern about the number of crimes committed by teenagers, from shoplifting and vandalism to more serious violence. This essay will discuss the main causes of youth crime and suggest some ways to reduce it.

Family problems are often at the root of the issue. Teenagers who grow up without consistent care, guidance or supervision, perhaps because their parents work long hours or the family is going through conflict, are more likely to look for attention and belonging elsewhere, sometimes in gangs. Poverty and lack of opportunity also play a part: young people in deprived areas who see little chance of a good education or job may turn to crime as a quick way to obtain money or status. Peer pressure, boredom and online content that glamorises violence can further encourage risky behaviour.

To tackle this problem, prevention is more effective than punishment. Local authorities should provide youth centres, sports clubs and arts programmes that give teenagers somewhere safe to go and positive role models, particularly in the evenings and during school holidays. Schools can identify students at risk early and offer counselling and mentoring, while parenting support programmes can help struggling families. For young people who have already offended, rehabilitation through education, training and community work is more likely to change their behaviour than prison, which often brings them into contact with more experienced criminals.

In conclusion, youth crime is largely caused by family difficulties, poverty and negative influences. By investing in activities for young people, early support in schools and rehabilitation rather than harsh punishment, societies can help teenagers choose a better path in life.

A large share of all the food produced in the world is never eaten, while millions of people do not have enough to eat. This essay will explain why so much food is wasted and suggest how the problem can be reduced.

Waste occurs at every stage of the food supply chain. On farms, crops may be left unharvested because prices are too low, or rejected because they do not meet supermarkets' strict standards for size and appearance. In developing countries, a lack of proper storage and refrigeration means that much food spoils before it reaches consumers. In wealthy countries, however, the largest amount is wasted by shops, restaurants and households. Supermarkets encourage people to buy more than they need through multi-buy offers, many consumers misunderstand 'best before' dates and throw away food that is still safe to eat, and restaurants often serve portions that are too large.

Several solutions could make a significant difference. Governments could require large supermarkets to donate unsold but edible food to charities, as some European countries already do, and invest in storage and cold-chain facilities in developing regions. Retailers should relax cosmetic standards and sell imperfect fruit and vegetables at lower prices, while clearer date labels would help consumers understand when food is genuinely unsafe. At home, people can reduce waste by planning meals, buying only what they need and using leftovers creatively. Unavoidable food waste could also be collected separately and turned into compost or energy.

In conclusion, food waste is caused by commercial standards, poor storage and careless consumer habits. Through regulation, changes in retail practice and more thoughtful shopping, much of this waste could be prevented.

Across the world, traditional crafts such as hand weaving, pottery and woodcarving are practised by fewer and fewer people, and in some places they are close to disappearing. This essay will look at the reasons for this decline and suggest ways to preserve these skills.

The main cause is competition from mass production. Factory-made goods are much cheaper and quicker to produce than handmade items, so craftspeople struggle to earn a decent living from their work. As a result, young people in craft villages often see little future in the family trade and move to cities in search of better-paid jobs. Another reason is that traditional skills are usually passed down informally from parents to children over many years, and when the younger generation is no longer interested, this chain of knowledge is broken. Changing tastes also play a role, as many consumers prefer modern, standardised products to traditional designs.

There are several ways to keep these crafts alive. Governments and cultural organisations could provide grants and training programmes so that master craftspeople can teach apprentices and earn an income while doing so. Crafts could also be included in school art lessons, giving children an early appreciation of their cultural heritage. In addition, linking crafts with tourism, through workshops where visitors can watch and try traditional techniques, can create new sources of income. Finally, online marketplaces and collaborations with modern designers can help artisans reach customers around the world and adapt traditional products to contemporary tastes.

In conclusion, traditional crafts are declining because of cheap factory goods, a lack of young successors and changing tastes. With financial support, education, tourism and modern marketing, these valuable skills can be preserved for future generations.

Thân 2 (giải pháp): tăng kinh phí xét nghiệm đột xuất, lưu mẫu để kiểm tra lại; phạt nặng, nhất quán (cấm thi đấu, thu hồi huy chương), phạt cả HLV; giáo dục từ sớm về sức khoẻ và đạo đức
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: Winning brings fame and sponsorship deals.
Agencies should carry out unannounced tests.
Retesting old samples acts as a strong deterrent.
sự trong sạch của thể thao
Tough penalties protect the integrity of sport.
writing.sample:
Despite strict rules and regular testing, some professional athletes continue to use banned substances to improve their performance. This essay will consider why athletes take this risk and what can be done to stop it.

The main reason is the enormous reward for success at the highest level. Winning a major championship can bring fame, sponsorship deals and millions of dollars, while athletes who finish just outside the medal positions may receive very little. When the difference between first and fourth place is a fraction of a second, some competitors are tempted to look for any advantage, even an illegal one. Pressure from coaches, sponsors and sometimes even national sports organisations can make this temptation stronger, especially if athletes believe that their rivals are also cheating. In addition, new drugs and methods are constantly being developed, and some athletes believe they will not be caught.

Several measures could reduce doping. Firstly, anti-doping agencies need sufficient funding to carry out frequent, unannounced tests and to develop new detection methods. Storing samples for many years, so that they can be retested when better technology becomes available, also acts as a strong deterrent. Secondly, punishments should be severe and consistent, including long bans and the return of prize money and medals, and they should extend to coaches and officials who organise doping. Thirdly, education programmes should begin at a young age, teaching athletes about both the health risks and the ethical importance of fair competition.

In conclusion, athletes use performance-enhancing drugs mainly because of the huge rewards and pressures of elite sport. More effective testing, tougher penalties and better education are the best ways to protect the integrity of sport.

writing.title: Young people leaving the countryside
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, young people are leaving rural areas to live and work in cities.

What problems does this cause? What can be done to solve these problems?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: người trẻ rời nông thôn ra thành phố + nêu vấn đề và giải pháp

Thân 1 (vấn đề): nông thôn già hoá, dân số giảm, người già thiếu người chăm; trường, trạm y tế, xe buýt đóng cửa → vòng luẩn quẩn; thiếu lao động nông nghiệp, mất tri thức truyền thống; thành phố quá tải

Thân 2 (giải pháp): internet tốc độ cao để làm việc từ xa; vay ưu đãi cho nông dân trẻ, doanh nghiệp nông thôn (chế biến, du lịch sinh thái); nâng cấp trường, y tế, giao thông; ưu đãi cho bác sĩ, giáo viên về nông thôn
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: Rural bus services become uneconomical and close.
Cities face pressure from the arrival of migrants.
Grants could support small rural enterprises.
Eco-tourism creates jobs in the countryside.
Tax breaks can attract doctors to rural areas.
Better infrastructure could help the countryside thrive.
writing.sample:
In many countries, villages are emptying as young people move to cities in search of education, jobs and a more exciting lifestyle. This trend creates serious problems for rural areas, but there are ways in which governments could respond.

The most immediate effect is an ageing and shrinking rural population. When young adults leave, villages are left mainly with elderly residents, many of whom need care but have no family nearby to help them. As the population falls, schools, health centres, shops and bus services become uneconomical and close, which makes rural life even less attractive and encourages more people to leave. Agriculture also suffers, because there are too few workers to farm the land, and traditional knowledge about local crops and customs may be lost. At the same time, the cities that receive these migrants face overcrowding, rising housing costs and pressure on public services.

To address these problems, governments should make rural areas better places to live and work. Investment in fast internet connections would allow people to work remotely or run online businesses from the countryside. Grants and low-interest loans could support young farmers and small rural enterprises, including food processing and eco-tourism, which create well-paid jobs. Improving local schools, clinics and transport links is also essential, as families will only stay if they have access to good basic services. Some countries also offer incentives, such as cheap housing or tax breaks, to attract professionals like doctors and teachers to rural communities.

In conclusion, the movement of young people to cities leaves rural areas ageing, poorer and short of services. Better infrastructure, support for rural businesses and incentives for skilled workers could help the countryside to thrive again.

writing.title: Smaller families
writing.prompt:

In many countries, people are choosing to have fewer children, or none at all.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.

Thân 1 (vì sao): chi phí nuôi con (nhà ở, học hành, trông trẻ) tăng; phụ nữ học cao, theo đuổi sự nghiệp, sinh con muộn; quan niệm sinh con là lựa chọn cá nhân; giờ làm dài, thiếu hỗ trợ
Thân 2 (tích cực hay tiêu cực): cá nhân – con được đầu tư nhiều hơn, cha mẹ tự do hơn; xã hội – dân số già, áp lực lương hưu và y tế, thiếu lao động, nông thôn vắng người

writing.sample:
In many parts of the world, birth rates have fallen sharply, and more couples are deciding to have only one child or none at all. This trend reflects major economic and social changes, and while it brings some benefits to individuals, I believe its overall effect on society is negative.

There are several reasons for this change. The cost of raising a child, including housing, education and childcare, has risen considerably, especially in cities, so many couples feel they can only afford one child. Women today are far better educated and more likely to pursue careers, and many choose to delay starting a family, which often results in fewer children. In addition, attitudes have changed: having children is increasingly seen as a personal choice rather than a duty, and some people prefer to focus on travel, personal development or their relationship. Long working hours and a lack of support for working parents also make family life seem difficult to manage.

For individuals, smaller families can mean more resources and attention for each child, and greater freedom for parents. At a national level, however, the consequences are worrying. A low birth rate leads to an ageing population, with fewer workers paying taxes to support a growing number of retired people, which places enormous pressure on pension and healthcare systems. In the long term, labour shortages may slow economic growth, and some rural areas may become almost empty.

In conclusion, people are having fewer children mainly because of high costs, changing roles for women and new attitudes towards family life. Although this can benefit individual families, it is a negative development for society as a whole, and governments should make it easier for those who want children to have them, for example through affordable childcare and generous parental leave.

writing.title: Young people reading less for pleasure
writing.prompt:

Fewer young people read books for pleasure today than in the past.

Why is this the case? What can be done to encourage young people to read more?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: giới trẻ đọc sách giải trí ít hơn + nêu sẽ giải thích nguyên nhân và cách khuyến khích
Thân 1 (vì sao): giải trí số (video ngắn, game, mạng xã hội) kích thích tức thì; khó tập trung đọc dài; sách gắn với bài vở, thi cử; lịch học dày đặc

Thân 2 (giải pháp): giờ đọc sách tự chọn ở trường, không kiểm tra; thư viện có sách hợp sở thích (truyện tranh, khoa học viễn tưởng); cha mẹ làm gương, không để màn hình trong phòng ngủ; e-book, sách nói, cộng đồng đọc online
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: tác phẩm bắt buộc trong chương trình
Students mainly read set texts for exams.
Schools could set aside time for free reading.

Parents can set an example by reading themselves.
Young people can rediscover the pleasure of reading.
writing.sample:
It is widely reported that children and teenagers today read far fewer books for enjoyment than previous generations did. This essay will explain why this is happening and suggest ways to encourage young people to read more.

The main reason is competition from digital entertainment. Smartphones offer an endless supply of short videos, games and social media posts that provide instant stimulation, and compared with these, a book can seem slow and demanding. Because many apps are designed to capture attention for as long as possible, young people may also find it harder to concentrate on long texts. Another reason is that reading is often associated with school. When students mainly read set texts in order to answer exam questions, they may come to see books as work rather than pleasure. Busy timetables, homework and extra classes also leave little free time.

Several measures could help reverse this trend. Schools could set aside time each day for students to read books of their own choice, without tests or written summaries, so that reading feels enjoyable rather than compulsory. Well-stocked school and public libraries, with books on topics that interest teenagers, such as sport, science fiction or graphic novels, are also important. At home, parents can set an example by reading themselves and by keeping screens out of bedrooms at night. Finally, technology itself can be part of the solution: e-books, audiobooks and online reading communities can attract young people who might never pick up a printed book.

In conclusion, young people read less mainly because of digital distractions and the link between books and schoolwork. Giving them free choice, better libraries, good role models and digital options could help them rediscover the pleasure of reading.

writing.title: Paying more for famous brands
writing.prompt:

Write at least 250 words.

Kết bài: tóm tắt

Designer products are symbols of wealth.
người có sức ảnh hưởng trên mạng

Luxury brands can charge many times more than ordinary manufacturers for similar items, yet their products remain extremely popular. This essay will discuss why people buy expensive branded goods and how this affects both individuals and society.

The most important reason is the desire for status. Designer products are widely recognised symbols of wealth and success, so owning them allows people to show others what they have achieved and to feel part of a particular social group. Social media has strengthened this motivation, as people share images of their lifestyles, and celebrities and influencers constantly display luxury items. Some buyers are also attracted by genuine qualities, such as superior materials, skilled craftsmanship and durability, believing that one well-made product is better than several cheap ones. For others, buying a famous brand is simply a way of rewarding themselves after years of hard work.

The effects of this trend are mixed. For individuals, a luxury purchase can bring pleasure and confidence, and well-made items may last for many years. However, people who feel pressure to keep up with others may spend beyond their means, sometimes falling into debt to buy goods they cannot really afford. At the level of society, the luxury industry creates jobs in design, manufacturing and retail, and it helps to preserve traditional skills such as leatherwork and watchmaking. On the other hand, the constant display of expensive possessions can encourage materialism and make inequality more visible, leaving those who cannot afford such items feeling excluded.

In conclusion, people buy luxury brands mainly to signal status, but also for quality and personal satisfaction. While the industry brings economic benefits, excessive spending on branded goods can cause financial problems and reinforce materialistic values.

In recent years, second-hand clothing shops and resale apps have become increasingly popular, particularly among young shoppers. This essay will consider the reasons for this trend and argue that it should be actively encouraged.

Several factors explain the growing interest in used clothing. The first is cost: rising living expenses have made many young people more careful with money, and second-hand items allow them to buy good-quality or even designer clothes at a fraction of the original price. The second is environmental awareness. Many young consumers now know that the fashion industry uses huge amounts of water and energy and that millions of tonnes of clothing are thrown away every year, so buying used items feels like a responsible choice. Technology has also made second-hand shopping easier, as online platforms allow people to search for, buy and sell clothes quickly from their phones. Finally, vintage fashion has become stylish, and unique second-hand pieces allow people to express their individuality.

I believe this trend deserves strong support. Extending the life of clothing is one of the simplest ways to reduce the environmental impact of fashion, since every garment that is reused means one fewer needs to be produced. It also helps people on lower incomes to dress well, and many second-hand shops are run by charities, so purchases support good causes. Governments could encourage the trend by reducing taxes on repair and resale businesses, while schools and the media could promote clothes swaps and repair skills. Some critics worry that the trend harms clothing manufacturers, but the benefits to the environment and to consumers are far greater.

In conclusion, second-hand clothing is popular because it is affordable, environmentally friendly, convenient and fashionable. Given these benefits, it is a trend that should be encouraged.

writing.title: Stress and anxiety among teenagers
writing.prompt:

writing.sample:
Surveys in many countries suggest that teenagers today experience more stress and anxiety than earlier generations. This essay will examine the main reasons for this and suggest what parents and schools can do to support young people.

One major source of pressure is education. In competitive systems, teenagers are expected to achieve high grades, win places at top universities and build impressive records of extracurricular activities, often while attending extra classes in the evenings and at weekends. Many fear that a single poor exam result could ruin their future. A second factor is social media. Young people constantly compare themselves with the carefully edited lives of their peers and of celebrities, which can damage their self-esteem, and online bullying can follow them home in a way that playground arguments once did not. Uncertainty about the future, including concerns about jobs, housing and climate change, adds to their worries.

Parents and schools both have an important role to play. Parents can help by keeping their expectations realistic, praising effort rather than only results and making time to talk openly with their children about their feelings. Setting limits on phone use, particularly at night, can also improve sleep and reduce exposure to harmful comparisons. Schools, meanwhile, should employ trained counsellors and teach students practical strategies for managing stress, such as time management, exercise and mindfulness. They could also reduce unnecessary testing and give more value to creativity, sport and personal development rather than exam scores alone.

In conclusion, teenage stress is mainly caused by academic pressure, social media and anxiety about the future. With realistic expectations at home and better mental health support at school, young people can develop the resilience they need to cope.

writing.sample:
In the past, many people stayed with the same employer or profession for their whole working lives, but today it is common to change jobs frequently and even to switch to completely different careers. This essay will explain why this is happening and identify the skills people need to make such changes successfully.

The main reason is the speed of economic and technological change. New industries are constantly emerging while others shrink, and automation has replaced many routine tasks, so workers sometimes have no choice but to move into new fields. Employers also offer less job security than before, relying more on short-term contracts, which encourages people to look for better opportunities elsewhere. At the same time, attitudes towards work have changed. Younger generations often expect their jobs to be meaningful and enjoyable, and if a role no longer satisfies them, they are willing to leave. Longer working lives also mean that people have more time to explore different paths.

To change careers successfully, the most important skill is the ability to keep learning. People who can teach themselves new knowledge, whether through online courses, evening classes or practical experience, adapt far more easily to unfamiliar roles. Transferable skills, such as communication, problem-solving and digital literacy, are also essential, because they are valued in almost every industry and allow people to build on their previous experience. In addition, career changers need networking skills to make contacts in a new field, and resilience to cope with the uncertainty and lower status that may come with starting again.

In conclusion, frequent career changes result from rapid economic change, reduced job security and new attitudes towards work. Those who are willing to keep learning, develop transferable skills and build strong networks are most likely to succeed.

writing.title: More people cycling to work

In a number of cities around the world, bicycles are becoming a more common sight on the way to offices and schools. This essay will discuss why cycling has grown in popularity and how governments could encourage even more people to cycle.

There are several reasons for this trend. Firstly, many people now see cycling as a way to stay healthy. With more jobs involving long hours at a desk, cycling to work allows people to build exercise into their daily routine without having to visit a gym. Secondly, cycling is cheap and often fast: in congested city centres, a bicycle can be quicker than a car or bus, and riders avoid fuel and parking costs. Thirdly, growing concern about climate change and air pollution has encouraged people to choose transport that produces no emissions. The spread of electric bicycles and bike-sharing schemes has also made cycling practical for people who live further away or do not own a bike.

Governments can do a great deal to build on this trend. The most important measure is to provide safe, continuous cycle lanes that are physically separated from traffic, since fear of accidents is the main reason many people do not cycle. Secure bicycle parking at stations, schools and workplaces is also necessary, as is the expansion of affordable bike-sharing systems. In addition, governments could offer subsidies for buying bicycles and electric bikes, and employers could be encouraged to provide showers and changing facilities. Lower speed limits in residential areas would also make roads safer for everyone.

In conclusion, cycling is becoming more popular because it is healthy, economical and environmentally friendly. With safer infrastructure and practical incentives, governments could make it an everyday choice for many more people.

writing.title: Fewer people volunteering

Write about the following topic:

Why might this be? How could more people be encouraged to volunteer?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

outline: Mở bài: các tổ chức khó tìm tình nguyện viên + nêu nội dung
Thân 1 (vì sao): thiếu thời gian (giờ làm dài, chăm con, chăm cha mẹ); áp lực tài chính → làm thêm có lương; cộng đồng kém gắn kết; thủ tục rườm rà, yêu cầu cam kết lâu dài

Thân 2 (khuyến khích): cơ hội linh hoạt (sự kiện một lần, dự án ngắn, việc online); công ty cho ngày nghỉ có lương để tình nguyện; trường học tổ chức dự án cộng đồng; ghi nhận (chứng nhận, thư giới thiệu)
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: Fewer people are willing to give their time.
Some volunteers are put off by long application forms.
Many people cannot commit to regular hours.
sự kiện diễn ra một lần
One-off events suit people with busy lives.
Volunteering days are part of companies' social responsibility programmes.
Recognition encourages more people to get involved.
writing.sample:
Charities, sports clubs and community groups in many places report that fewer people are willing to give their time without payment. This essay will consider why this may be happening and suggest ways to encourage more people to volunteer.

The most likely reason is a lack of time. Many adults work long hours, commute long distances and have responsibilities for children or elderly relatives, so they have little energy left for voluntary activities. Financial pressure plays a part as well: when living costs rise, people may take on extra paid work rather than unpaid roles. In addition, communities are less close-knit than in the past. People move home more often and may not know their neighbours, so they feel less connected to local organisations. Finally, some potential volunteers are put off by formal procedures, such as long application forms and training requirements, or by the expectation that they must commit to regular hours for a long period.

There are several ways to reverse this trend. Organisations could offer more flexible opportunities, such as one-off events, short projects or tasks that can be done online, which suit people with busy lives. Employers could give staff a few paid volunteering days each year, which many companies already do as part of their social responsibility programmes. Schools and universities can introduce young people to volunteering through community projects, helping them to develop skills and a lasting habit. Recognition also matters: certificates, references for job applications and public appreciation can show volunteers that their contribution is valued.

In conclusion, volunteering may be declining because people have less time, face financial pressure and feel less connected to their communities. Flexible opportunities, support from employers and schools, and greater recognition could encourage many more people to get involved.

writing.title: Streaming at home or going to the cinema?
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Many people now prefer to watch films at home using online streaming services rather than going to the cinema.

Why is this? Do you think cinemas will disappear in the future?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: xem phim tại nhà qua nền tảng trực tuyến tăng mạnh + trả lời: rạp sẽ thay đổi nhưng khó biến mất
Thân 1 (vì sao): tiện (chọn phim bất cứ lúc nào, tạm dừng, nhiều thiết bị); rẻ hơn; thiết bị gia đình tốt; phim lên mạng sớm

Thân 2 (rạp có biến mất không): không – xem phim ở rạp là hoạt động xã hội, cảm xúc chung của khán giả; màn hình lớn, âm thanh mạnh, không bị xao nhãng; rạp đang thích nghi (ghế cao cấp, định dạng đặc biệt, chiếu hoà nhạc, thể thao)
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: nền tảng xem phim trực tuyến
Streaming platforms offer thousands of films.
A monthly subscription costs less than a cinema trip.
Many films appear online soon after their cinema release.
Cinemas will survive, albeit in a changed form.
writing.sample:
With the rapid growth of online streaming platforms, a large number of people now choose to watch films on their sofas rather than in cinemas. This essay will explain the reasons for this preference and argue that, although cinemas will change, they are unlikely to disappear.

The main attraction of streaming is convenience. Viewers can choose from thousands of films and series at any time, pause whenever they like and watch on a television, laptop or phone. It is also much cheaper: a monthly subscription often costs less than a single family trip to the cinema, once tickets, transport and snacks are included. Improvements in home technology, such as large high-definition screens and sound systems, mean that the viewing experience at home is now very good. Furthermore, many new films appear online soon after their cinema release, so there is less reason to wait in queues or sit among noisy strangers.

Nevertheless, I do not believe cinemas will disappear. Going to the cinema is a social event, a way for friends, couples and families to spend time together outside the home, and many people value the shared excitement of watching a film with a large audience. Cinemas also offer an experience that is hard to recreate at home, with giant screens, powerful sound and no distractions from phones or household tasks. Many cinemas are already adapting by offering comfortable seating, premium formats and better food and drink, as well as screenings of concerts and sports events.

In conclusion, streaming services are popular because they are convenient, affordable and of high quality. However, cinemas provide a social and immersive experience that streaming cannot fully replace, so they are likely to survive, albeit in a changed form.

writing.title: Too many graduates, too few tradespeople
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In some countries, many young people go to university even though there are not enough graduate jobs, while there is a shortage of workers in skilled trades such as plumbing and electrical work.

Why is this happening? What can be done to solve this problem?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: đại học đông nghẹt trong khi thiếu thợ ống nước, thợ điện; nhiều cử nhân làm việc không cần bằng + nêu nội dung
Thân 1 (vì sao): bằng đại học có địa vị cao, định kiến với nghề tay chân; cha mẹ, nhà trường hướng con vào đại học; hướng nghiệp thiên về học thuật; trường nghề thiếu đầu tư
Thân 2 (giải pháp): đầu tư giáo dục nghề chất lượng, liên kết doanh nghiệp; học nghề có lương; hướng nghiệp cân bằng (mời thợ giỏi chia sẻ, thông tin thu nhập); lộ trình học lên, khởi nghiệp
Kết bài: tóm tắt
vocab: các nghề kỹ thuật lành nghề
There is a shortage of workers in skilled trades.
A degree carries a higher social status.
Careers advice tends to focus on university.
Governments should invest in vocational education.
Clear routes for progression would change attitudes.
writing.sample:
In a number of countries, universities are full while employers struggle to find qualified plumbers, electricians and mechanics. At the same time, many graduates end up in jobs that do not require a degree. This essay will examine why this imbalance exists and how it could be corrected.

The main cause is the higher social status attached to a university degree. In many cultures, going to university is seen as the only route to a respectable, well-paid career, while practical trades are wrongly regarded as suitable only for students who fail academically. Parents often encourage their children to choose university for this reason, and schools are sometimes judged by how many students they send there. Careers advice also tends to focus on academic pathways, so many teenagers know little about the training, earnings and opportunities available in skilled trades. In addition, vocational colleges in some countries are underfunded and have poor facilities, which makes them less attractive.

Several steps could help to solve this problem. Governments should invest in high-quality vocational education, with modern equipment and close links to employers, and promote it as an equally valuable choice. Paid apprenticeships, in which young people earn a salary while learning a trade, would be especially attractive to students worried about the cost of university. Schools should provide balanced careers guidance, including visits from tradespeople and information about the strong demand and good salaries in these fields. Finally, creating clear routes for progression, so that skilled workers can later gain higher qualifications or start their own businesses, would help to change attitudes.

In conclusion, the shortage of skilled tradespeople results mainly from the low status of vocational training and a lack of information. Better funding, paid apprenticeships and fairer careers advice could create a better balance in the workforce.

writing.title: Robots caring for the elderly
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In some countries, robots and artificial intelligence are being used to help care for elderly people.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: dân số già, thiếu người chăm sóc → dùng robot, AI + quan điểm: tích cực nếu hỗ trợ chứ không thay thế con người
Thân 1 (tích cực): lấp chỗ thiếu điều dưỡng; robot làm việc nặng (nâng bệnh nhân); AI nhắc uống thuốc, đo nhịp tim, phát hiện té ngã; giúp người già sống độc lập ở nhà
Thân 2 (lo ngại): người già cần bầu bạn, tình cảm; dùng robot để cắt chi phí → cô đơn, trầm cảm; quyền riêng tư dữ liệu sức khoẻ; khó dùng công nghệ mới
Thân 3 (đánh giá): lợi ích lớn hơn nếu robot làm việc lặp lại, người chăm sóc có thêm thời gian trò chuyện
Kết bài: tích cực, miễn là bổ trợ con người và bảo vệ phẩm giá, quyền riêng tư
vocab: The number of care workers fails to keep up with demand.
Robots can take over physically demanding tasks.
AI systems can detect falls and alert doctors.
Elderly people need companionship as well as care.
Strict rules should protect patients' dignity.
writing.sample:
As populations age and the number of care workers fails to keep up with demand, some countries have begun using robots and artificial intelligence to help look after older people. I believe this is largely a positive development, provided that technology supports human carers rather than replacing them.

The main argument in favour is that technology can fill a growing gap in care. In many societies, there are simply not enough nurses and carers for the rising number of elderly people, and those who work in the sector are often overworked. Robots can take over physically demanding tasks, such as lifting patients out of bed, while AI systems can remind people to take their medication, monitor their heart rate and detect falls, alerting family members or doctors immediately. Such tools allow older people to live independently in their own homes for longer, which most of them prefer.

There are, however, legitimate concerns. Elderly people need companionship and emotional support as well as physical care, and no machine can truly replace a caring human relationship. If governments and care homes use robots mainly to cut costs, older people might spend long periods with little human contact, which could increase loneliness and depression. There are also worries about privacy, since monitoring devices collect sensitive information about people's health and daily lives, and about whether older users can operate unfamiliar technology.

On balance, I believe the benefits outweigh these risks if technology is used wisely. By handling routine and physical tasks, robots and AI can free human carers to spend more time talking with and comforting the people they look after.

In conclusion, using robots and AI in elderly care is a positive development, as long as it complements human care and strict rules protect patients' dignity and privacy.

writing.title: Earning a living through apps
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

More and more people now earn a living through short-term jobs arranged by apps, such as delivering food or driving passengers, instead of having a permanent job with one employer.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: nhiều người kiếm sống qua ứng dụng (giao đồ ăn, chở khách) thay vì việc cố định + quan điểm: phần lớn tiêu cực ở hình thức hiện nay
Thân 1 (tích cực): linh hoạt giờ giấc, hợp với sinh viên, cha mẹ, người làm thêm; dễ bắt đầu, nguồn thu cho người khó tìm việc; tiện, rẻ cho người dùng

Thân 2 (tiêu cực): bị coi là lao động tự do → không lương tối thiểu, nghỉ ốm, lương hưu; thu nhập phụ thuộc thuật toán; giờ làm dài, rủi ro giao thông; phần mềm quyết định sa thải; xã hội mất nguồn thu thuế
Thân 3 (đánh giá): có thể tích cực nếu luật bắt buộc thu nhập tối thiểu, bảo hiểm tai nạn, đóng góp lương hưu
Kết bài: tiêu cực nếu không có quy định chặt hơn
vocab: nền kinh tế việc làm tự do, ngắn hạn qua ứng dụng
The gig economy has grown rapidly.
việc làm truyền thống, ổn định
Some people struggle to find conventional employment.
lao động tự do, tự kinh doanh
Gig workers are usually classed as self-employed.
Many riders receive no sick pay.
The spread of insecure work affects tax revenue.
writing.sample:
Millions of people now earn money by delivering meals, driving passengers or completing small tasks through smartphone apps, rather than working for a single employer. Although this 'gig economy' offers flexibility, I believe it is a largely negative development in its current form.

Supporters of app-based work emphasise its flexibility. Workers can choose when and how much they work, which suits students, parents and people who want to earn extra income alongside another job. The apps also make it easy to start working quickly, with few formal requirements, which can provide a valuable source of income for people who struggle to find conventional employment, such as recent migrants. For consumers, these services are convenient and often cheap.

However, this flexibility comes at a high price for many workers. Because they are usually classed as self-employed, gig workers often have no guaranteed minimum wage, sick pay, holiday pay or pension, and their income can fall suddenly if the company changes its rates or algorithms. Many must work very long hours to earn a reasonable living, and delivery riders face significant risks on busy roads without proper insurance. Moreover, decisions about pay and even dismissal may be made by software, leaving workers with little opportunity to complain or negotiate. For society, the spread of insecure work can mean lower tax revenue and more people without savings for old age.

In my view, the gig economy could become positive if governments required platforms to provide basic protections, such as minimum earnings, accident insurance and pension contributions, while preserving flexible hours.

In conclusion, while app-based work offers flexibility and convenience, the lack of security and rights for workers makes it a negative development overall unless stronger regulation is introduced.

writing.title: The growth of megacities
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

An increasing proportion of the world's population now lives in very large cities with more than ten million inhabitants.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: siêu đô thị (Tokyo, Delhi, Lagos...) ngày càng nhiều + quan điểm: tích cực nói chung

Thân 1 (tích cực): tập trung doanh nghiệp, lao động, đại học → ý tưởng lan nhanh, kinh tế tăng trưởng; lương cao, y tế, giáo dục tốt hơn; hiệu quả – chi phí dịch vụ trên đầu người thấp, ít năng lượng cho đi lại
Thân 2 (tiêu cực): tăng trưởng quá nhanh → khu ổ chuột, kẹt xe, ô nhiễm; chi phí sống cao, bất bình đẳng; căng thẳng, cô đơn
Thân 3 (đánh giá): vấn đề do quy hoạch kém chứ không do quy mô; đầu tư giao thông công cộng, nhà ở giá rẻ, mảng xanh
Kết bài: tích cực nếu được quản lý tốt
vocab: The number of megacities continues to grow.
phần lớn hơn so với tỉ lệ dân số
Large cities produce a disproportionate share of national wealth.
giúp các gia đình thoát nghèo
City jobs can lift families out of poverty.
Rapid growth can lead to slums.
Inequality between neighbourhoods can be stark.
writing.sample:
Cities such as Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and Lagos now have populations larger than many countries, and the number of these megacities continues to grow. Although their rapid growth causes serious problems, I believe the concentration of people in very large cities is, on the whole, a positive development.

The main advantage of megacities is economic. When large numbers of businesses, workers and universities are concentrated in one place, ideas spread quickly, companies find the skilled staff they need and new industries develop. This is why large cities usually produce a disproportionate share of national wealth and offer higher wages than rural areas. For individuals, moving to a big city can provide access to better jobs, hospitals and education, and lift families out of poverty. Large cities can also be more efficient: when people live close together, public transport, water supply and other services can be provided at a lower cost per person, and residents of dense cities often use less energy for travel than those in suburbs.

However, the problems are undeniable. When growth is too rapid, housing, roads and public services cannot keep up, leading to slums, traffic congestion, air pollution and long commutes. Living costs in megacities are often extremely high, and inequality between rich and poor neighbourhoods can be stark. Some residents also experience stress and isolation despite being surrounded by millions of people.

In my view, these difficulties are mainly the result of poor planning rather than of city size itself. With investment in public transport, affordable housing and green spaces, megacities can become healthier and fairer places to live.

In conclusion, despite congestion, pollution and high costs, the economic opportunities and efficiency of megacities make their growth a positive development, as long as it is properly managed.

writing.title: Messaging instead of talking
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Many people, especially young people, now prefer to communicate through text messages and social media rather than by talking on the phone or meeting face to face.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: giới trẻ thích nhắn tin hơn gọi điện, gặp mặt + quan điểm: tiêu cực nếu phụ thuộc quá nhiều
Thân 1 (lý do/lợi ích): nhanh, rẻ, tiện, trả lời khi rảnh; có thời gian suy nghĩ, đỡ áp lực cho người nhút nhát; giữ liên lạc với nhiều người, kể cả ở nước ngoài
Thân 2 (bất lợi): mất giọng điệu, nét mặt, ngôn ngữ cơ thể → hiểu lầm, mâu thuẫn leo thang; thiếu kỹ năng xã hội (lắng nghe, đọc cảm xúc, nói tự tin); không thoả mãn nhu cầu kết nối → cô đơn
Thân 3 (đề xuất): nhắn tin để bổ sung chứ không thay thế; khuyến khích nói chuyện trực tiếp khi việc quan trọng
Kết bài: tiêu cực
vocab: Body language is lost in text messages.
Minor disagreements can escalate into serious conflicts.
đọc được cảm xúc của người khác
Young people need to learn to read other people's emotions.
Face-to-face interaction satisfies our need for connection.
bổ sung chứ không thay thế
Messages should complement, not replace, real conversations.
writing.sample:
For many people today, especially the young, sending a message is far more common than making a phone call or meeting in person. While text-based communication has clear advantages, I believe that relying on it too heavily is a negative development.

There are understandable reasons for this preference. Messages are quick, cheap and convenient: they can be sent at any time and answered when the recipient is free, which suits busy lifestyles. Written communication also gives people time to think before they reply, which many shy or anxious individuals find less stressful than a live conversation. Social media and group chats make it easy to stay in touch with large numbers of friends and relatives, including those who live in other countries.

However, the disadvantages are significant. Much of the meaning in human communication comes from tone of voice, facial expressions and body language, all of which are lost in text. As a result, messages are frequently misunderstood, and minor disagreements can escalate into serious conflicts. More importantly, young people who mainly communicate through screens may have fewer opportunities to develop essential social skills, such as listening carefully, reading other people's emotions and speaking confidently, which are vital in job interviews, workplaces and close relationships. Online contact also seems to satisfy the human need for connection less fully than face-to-face interaction, so heavy reliance on messaging may contribute to loneliness despite constant contact.

For these reasons, text messages should complement, not replace, real conversations. Families and schools should encourage young people to talk in person, or at least to make a phone call, when an issue is important or sensitive.

In conclusion, although messaging is convenient and less stressful for some, its negative effects on understanding, social skills and relationships make the shift away from spoken communication a negative development.

writing.title: Young adults living with their parents
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many countries, young adults are living with their parents for longer than in the past, often until their late twenties or thirties.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: người trẻ ở với cha mẹ đến cuối 20, 30 tuổi + quan điểm: chủ yếu tích cực với gia đình dù phản ánh khó khăn kinh tế
Thân 1 (tích cực): tiết kiệm để mua nhà, trả nợ học phí, chọn việc phù hợp; gia đình gắn kết, chia sẻ việc nhà và chi phí, chăm sóc cha mẹ già; truyền thống nhiều thế hệ ở châu Á
Thân 2 (tiêu cực): chậm tự lập, thiếu kỹ năng sống, dựa dẫm; căng thẳng về riêng tư, lối sống; trì hoãn kết hôn, sinh con; phản ánh vấn đề nhà ở và việc làm
Thân 3 (đánh giá): khắc phục được nếu con cái đóng góp chi phí và tự chịu trách nhiệm
Kết bài: chủ yếu tích cực
vocab: trả hết khoản vay học phí
Living at home helps graduates pay off student loans.
ở bên cạnh, sẵn sàng giúp
Adult children are on hand to help ageing parents.
hộ gia đình nhiều thế hệ
Multigenerational households are traditional in much of Asia.
Some young adults lack important life skills.
Living at home does not have to mean dependence.
writing.sample:
In many countries, it has become normal for young adults to remain in their parents' home well into their late twenties or even thirties. Although this trend is partly a sign of economic difficulties, I believe it is a mainly positive development for the families involved.

The most obvious benefit is financial. With high rents and house prices, living at home allows young people to save money for a deposit on a home, pay off student loans or take time to find a job that suits their qualifications rather than accepting the first offer. Many families also find that living together strengthens their relationships. Parents and adult children can share household tasks and costs, and the younger generation is on hand to help as their parents grow older. In many cultures, including much of Asia, multigenerational households are traditional and are regarded as a source of support rather than a sign of failure.

Critics argue that staying at home for too long can delay independence. Young adults who have never had to manage a household budget, pay bills or cook for themselves may lack important life skills, and some may rely too heavily on their parents' support. Sharing a home can also cause tension, particularly over privacy and different lifestyles, and may delay marriage and having children. Furthermore, the trend often reflects real problems in the housing and labour markets that governments should address.

However, these drawbacks can be managed if adult children contribute to household expenses and take responsibility for their own lives. Living at home does not have to mean dependence.

In conclusion, while the trend is partly caused by unaffordable housing and can delay independence, its financial and family benefits make it a largely positive development.

writing.title: Spending on experiences, not possessions
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Many people today, especially young people, prefer to spend their money on experiences such as travel, concerts and eating out, rather than on material possessions.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: trước kia đo thành công bằng tài sản, nay giới trẻ chi tiền cho trải nghiệm + quan điểm: tích cực
Thân 1 (cá nhân): trải nghiệm mang lại hạnh phúc lâu hơn đồ vật; thường được chia sẻ → gắn kết; mở rộng tầm nhìn, kỹ năng mới
Thân 2 (môi trường, kinh tế): bớt sản xuất, bao bì, rác (trừ khi bay quá nhiều); hỗ trợ nhà hàng, nhà hát, du lịch
Thân 3 (lo ngại): tiêu nhiều mà không tiết kiệm cho tương lai; mạng xã hội biến trải nghiệm thành cuộc thi khoe ảnh → phụ thuộc lựa chọn cá nhân
Kết bài: tích cực
vocab: Many people value experiences over material possessions.
Spending on experiences creates jobs in service industries.
vì chính giá trị của nó
People should choose experiences for their own sake.
writing.sample:
In the past, success was often measured by what people owned, such as a large house, an expensive car or fashionable clothes. Today, however, many people, particularly the young, would rather spend their money on travel, concerts, restaurants and other experiences. I believe this is largely a positive development.

For individuals, experiences tend to bring more lasting happiness than possessions. A new phone or handbag gives pleasure for a short time, but people quickly become used to it, whereas memories of a trip abroad or a concert with friends can be enjoyed for years. Experiences are also usually shared with others, which strengthens friendships and family relationships. In addition, activities such as travelling, learning to cook or attending cultural events can broaden people's horizons and help them develop new skills and interests.

This shift may also benefit the environment and the economy. Buying fewer material goods means less manufacturing, packaging and waste, although this advantage is reduced if people take frequent long-haul flights. Spending on local restaurants, theatres and tourism supports many small businesses and creates jobs in service industries.

There are, nonetheless, some concerns. Some young people spend heavily on holidays and entertainment while failing to save for their future, such as buying a home or preparing for retirement. Social media can also turn experiences into a form of competition, with people choosing activities mainly to share photos online rather than for genuine enjoyment.

On balance, these problems depend on individual choices rather than on the trend itself. As long as people budget sensibly and choose experiences for their own sake, valuing experiences over possessions can lead to happier and more sustainable lives.

In conclusion, the preference for experiences over material goods is a positive development, bringing greater well-being and fewer environmental costs.

writing.title: Translation apps instead of language learning
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Translation apps have improved so much that many people now rely on them instead of learning foreign languages.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: ứng dụng dịch dùng AI dịch gần như tức thì, nhiều người dựa vào thay vì học ngoại ngữ + quan điểm: tiêu cực
Thân 1 (lợi ích của app): du lịch, kinh doanh không cần phiên dịch; người nhập cư hiểu giấy tờ, lời khuyên y tế; tiết kiệm thời gian, xoá rào cản

Thân 2 (vì sao tiêu cực): ngôn ngữ gắn với văn hoá, tư duy; quan hệ thật cần hội thoại tự nhiên; dịch máy sai (thành ngữ, chuyên ngành) → hiểu lầm nghiêm trọng (luật, y tế); học ngoại ngữ tốt cho trí não
Thân 3 (đề xuất): app là công cụ bổ trợ; trường học vẫn coi trọng ngoại ngữ
Kết bài: tiêu cực
vocab: Businesses can deal with customers without hiring interpreters.
Translation apps remove many language barriers.
thiếu tính cá nhân, xa cách
A conversation through a phone app feels impersonal.
a supplement rather than a substitute
công cụ bổ trợ chứ không phải thay thế
Apps should be a supplement rather than a substitute.
writing.sample:
Thanks to advances in artificial intelligence, translation apps can now convert speech and text between dozens of languages almost instantly, and many people rely on them instead of learning a foreign language. Although these tools are extremely useful, I believe that relying on them in place of language learning is a negative development.

There is no doubt that translation technology brings important benefits. Travellers can read menus, ask for directions and communicate with local people in countries whose languages they do not speak. Businesses can deal with international customers and partners without hiring interpreters, and migrants can understand official documents and medical advice in their new countries. For quick, practical exchanges, the apps save time and remove many barriers.

However, a translation app cannot replace the deeper benefits of learning a language. Language is closely connected to culture, humour and ways of thinking, and people who learn a foreign language gain an understanding of other societies that no machine can provide. Real relationships, whether friendships, business partnerships or marriages, depend on natural conversation, which becomes awkward and impersonal when every sentence must pass through a phone. Machine translations can also be inaccurate, particularly with idioms, specialist vocabulary or sensitive topics, and such errors can cause serious misunderstandings in fields such as law or medicine. Moreover, learning another language is widely believed to benefit the brain, improving memory and concentration.

For these reasons, translation apps should be seen as a supplement rather than a substitute. Schools should continue to give language learning a central place in the curriculum, while teaching students to use technology wisely.

In conclusion, although translation apps are convenient for travel and simple communication, relying on them instead of learning languages is a negative development, as it limits cultural understanding, personal relationships and cognitive development.

writing.title: English as a global language
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

English is increasingly used as the main language of international business, science and entertainment, and more and more people around the world are learning it.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: tiếng Anh thống trị kinh doanh, khoa học, internet, giải trí + quan điểm: chủ yếu tích cực
Thân 1 (tích cực): giao tiếp quốc tế dễ dàng → hợp tác, tri thức lan nhanh; cá nhân – việc làm quốc tế, du học, thông tin trực tuyến; du lịch, kết bạn, tăng hiểu biết lẫn nhau
Thân 2 (tiêu cực): đe doạ ngôn ngữ, văn hoá khác; ngôn ngữ thiểu số có nguy cơ biến mất; bất công – người bản ngữ có lợi thế
Thân 3 (đánh giá): song ngữ – tiếng Anh cho mục đích quốc tế, tiếng mẹ đẻ trong đời sống; nhà nước hỗ trợ cả hai
Kết bài: tích cực dù có rủi ro cho sự đa dạng ngôn ngữ
vocab: English has become the dominant language of science.
Speaking English opens doors to international jobs.
Many minority languages are in danger of disappearing.
Learning English does not mean abandoning your mother tongue.
The spread of English may threaten linguistic diversity.
writing.sample:
English has become the dominant language of international business, scientific research, the internet and popular entertainment, and hundreds of millions of people are learning it as a second language. Although this trend raises concerns about cultural diversity, I believe it is mainly a positive development.

The greatest benefit of a shared global language is easier communication. When scientists, business people and diplomats from different countries can understand one another directly, cooperation becomes faster and cheaper, and knowledge spreads more quickly. For individuals, speaking English opens doors to international jobs, study abroad and a vast range of information online, much of which is available only in English. It also allows people to travel more easily and to make friends from all over the world, which can promote tolerance and understanding between cultures.

On the other hand, critics argue that the spread of English threatens other languages and cultures. When young people consume mainly English-language films, music and social media, they may lose interest in their own languages, literature and traditions. Many minority languages are already in danger of disappearing, and with them unique ways of seeing the world. There is also a question of fairness, as native English speakers enjoy a natural advantage in international careers and academic publishing, while others must invest years of effort to reach the same level.

In my view, these risks can be managed. Learning English does not require people to abandon their mother tongue; most people can become bilingual, using English for international purposes and their own language at home and in cultural life. Governments should support both English education and the preservation of local languages.

In conclusion, despite some threats to linguistic diversity, the spread of English as a global language is a positive development because it improves communication, opportunities and international understanding.

writing.title: Personal data and targeted advertising
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

Technology companies collect large amounts of personal information about their users, such as their location, searches and purchases, and use it to show them targeted advertising.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: công ty công nghệ thu thập dữ liệu để quảng cáo cá nhân hoá + quan điểm: tiêu cực
Thân 1 (lợi ích): quảng cáo hiệu quả, kể cả với doanh nghiệp nhỏ; gợi ý phù hợp, tiết kiệm thời gian; dịch vụ miễn phí nhờ tiền quảng cáo

Thân 2 (bất lợi): người dùng không biết bị thu thập gì (điều khoản dài); dữ liệu bị bán, rò rỉ, tấn công → lừa đảo, đánh cắp danh tính; thao túng chi tiêu, chính trị; quyền lực tập trung vào vài tập đoàn
Thân 3 (đề xuất): đồng ý rõ ràng, giới hạn loại dữ liệu, phạt nặng khi lạm dụng
Kết bài: tiêu cực
vocab: Targeted advertising reaches the most likely customers.
Permissions are hidden in long terms and conditions.
Leaked data can lead to identity theft.
Detailed personal data creates a risk of manipulation.
Large corporations face limited public accountability.
Companies should obtain clear consent before collecting data.
writing.sample:
Every time people search the internet, use social media or shop online, technology companies record details about their behaviour and use this information to show them personalised advertisements. While this practice has some benefits, I believe it is a negative development overall.

Supporters of data collection argue that it benefits both companies and consumers. Targeted advertising allows businesses, including small ones, to reach the customers most likely to be interested in their products, which makes marketing more efficient. For users, personalised recommendations can save time by showing them relevant products, news and entertainment. Moreover, advertising income is what allows many online services, such as search engines, email and social networks, to be offered free of charge.

However, the disadvantages are more serious. Most users have little idea how much information is being collected about them, as permissions are hidden in long and complicated terms and conditions that few people read. Detailed profiles of people's habits, health, finances and political views can be sold, leaked or hacked, exposing individuals to fraud and identity theft. There is also a risk of manipulation: when companies know people's weaknesses and emotions, they can target them with advertisements designed to encourage unnecessary spending, or even with misleading political messages. Finally, the concentration of so much personal data in the hands of a few powerful corporations gives them enormous influence over society, with limited public accountability.

In my opinion, people should not have to give up their privacy in order to use essential online services. Governments should require companies to obtain clear consent before collecting data, limit the types of information that can be used for advertising and impose heavy fines for misuse.

In conclusion, although targeted advertising can make online services free and convenient, the threats it poses to privacy, security and personal freedom make it a negative development.

writing.title: Ordering food instead of cooking
writing.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

More and more people now order meals through food delivery apps or buy ready-made food instead of cooking at home.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
outline: Mở bài: ứng dụng giao đồ ăn, đồ ăn sẵn khiến người ta ít nấu ăn + quan điểm: tiêu cực
Thân 1 (lý do/lợi ích): tiết kiệm thời gian cho người bận rộn; món ăn đa dạng; việc làm cho nhà hàng, người giao hàng, giúp quán nhỏ có thêm khách
Thân 2 (tiêu cực): nhiều muối, đường, chất béo, khẩu phần lớn → béo phì, bệnh tim; tốn kém; rác nhựa, khí thải; mất bữa cơm gia đình; trẻ không học nấu ăn
Kết bài: tiêu cực, nên nấu ăn ở nhà thường xuyên hơn
vocab: chỉ với vài lần chạm màn hình
Meals can be ordered with a few taps on a phone.
Delivery apps offer a huge variety of cuisines.
Frequent ordering puts a strain on household budgets.
Some children never learn basic cooking skills.
writing.sample:
Food delivery apps have made it possible to order almost any meal with a few taps on a phone, and supermarkets offer a growing range of ready-made dishes. As a result, many people now cook at home far less often than in the past. Although this trend is convenient, I believe it is a negative development.

There are clear reasons why these services are popular. People who work long hours or study late may have little time or energy to shop for ingredients and cook, and ordering food allows them to eat a hot meal quickly. Delivery apps also offer a huge variety of cuisines, so people can enjoy dishes that would be difficult to prepare at home. In addition, the industry creates jobs for restaurant staff and delivery riders and helps small food businesses reach more customers.

However, the negative effects outweigh this convenience. Takeaway and ready-made meals usually contain more salt, sugar and fat than home-cooked food, and portions tend to be larger, so eating them regularly can contribute to obesity, heart disease and other health problems. Ordering food is also expensive, and frequent use can put a strain on household budgets. The environmental cost is considerable too, as each delivery generates plastic packaging and, often, vehicle emissions. Perhaps most importantly, cooking and eating together has traditionally been a time for families to share their day, and when everyone orders separate meals and eats in front of screens, this valuable time is lost. Children who rarely see food being prepared may also never learn basic cooking skills.

In conclusion, while food delivery apps and ready meals are convenient, their effects on health, budgets, the environment and family life make this trend a negative development, and people would benefit from cooking at home more often.
